1 Introduction
The CrystalBridge® Transformation module contains the following components:
Data
Trans-
formation
Streamlined
SNP Kyano DTS enables fast data extractions during 1:1 migrations
Client-independent objects can be moved to ensure a complete copy of all
data that is relevant for moving a system or client
Predefined migration templates enable secure out-of-the-box data extrac-
tions for various SAP applications
Transformation
Cockpit
Extensive repository of transformation objects covering the majority of a
typical transformation scope
Consolidate multiple projects into a single project using predefined migra-
tion rules
Migrate historical data
Transformation
Content
Guided procedure for transformations
Templates for transformation objects
Templates for the rule base
Downtime
Optimization
Significantly reduced downtime minimizes business interruption
Migrate data while the source system is up and running
Changes made to data in the source system during migration are recorded
Data
Consistency
Verification
Check migrated data records against their check tables and value tables
Determine inconsistencies due to missing customizing data or master data
Identify missing or incorrect migration rules
Automated
Testing
Automate functional tests and regression tests in SAP systems
Check application data and customizing settings after the transformation
Contains predefined SNP test objects that can be extended according to
customer requirements

1.1 Additional Information
This documentation is part of the product Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation. Read the cor-
responding chapter before working with Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation and always keep
the documentation close at hand.
Training Courses
We recommend a training course for our product. You can either take the course at our training
center or on-site in your company’s SAP® environment.
Internet: https://www.snpgroup.com/en/about-snp/company/snp-academy/
Support
Contact SNP Support if you require help installing or using Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation.
E-mail: support@snpgroup.com
Internet: https://support.snpgroup.com/
Changelogs
Further information will follow.
Copyright
Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation and all related documents are intellectual property of SNP
Schneider-Neureither & Partner SE.
1.2 Handling the Transmission of Personal Data
WARNING
The software provided by SNP is a transformation tool whose use and scope can involve
various types of data, including personal data, depending on the configuration.
Therefore, before using the software, it must be checked whether corresponding author-
ization to handle personal data exists. This process must be followed when using and
configuring the software.
The authorization must be granted by the system administrator or an authorized rep-
resentative of the system administrator.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter18

=====PAGE 19=====
1.3 Requesting SNP Support Services
You can request SNP Support services via the SNP Support Portal. If you do not have a user
yet, register a new user as explained below.
1.3.1 Requesting Support
Proceed as follows to request support:
1.
Open the SNP Support Portal.
2. Log in with your user data.
3. In the Service Desk Requests area, click Request Standard Support.
4. Fill out all the required fields. The more information you provide, the more precisely the
problem can be analyzed.
5. In the Help from SNPedia area, click Start SNPedia Search.
The window Search Result(s) in SNPedia opens and offers suggested solutions.
6. If none of the solutions from SNPedia match, click
Continue with ticket.
7. Optional: Add attachments.
8. In the Priority and Descriptions area, define the priority of the ticket and add a descrip-
tion.
9. Click
OK - Apply changes and close at the bottom right.
You have created a ticket and requested support.
1.3.2 Creating Users
Proceed as follows to register a new user:
1. Optional: Ask another SNP Support Portal user to create a new user.
a. They can do so by clicking Register New User for Customer in the Service Desk
Requests area.
b. Provide all the required information.
c. Confirm the request by clicking
OK - Apply changes and close.
2. Optional: Ask your SNP contact to create a new user. The document Creating a User for a
Customer in the SNP Support Portal serves as a reference.
You will receive an e-mail with a password.
3. Follow the instructions in the e-mail and complete the registration.
You have registered a new user.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter19

1.3.3 Creating a User for a Customer in the SNP Support Portal
To create other users, you need a user in the SNP Support Portal.
Proceed as follows during the registration:
1.3.3.1 Creating a User
1. Open the Support Portal at https://support.snpgroup.com/.
2. Click the tile Register new user for customers.
3. Click the plus icon (yellow) to select the project. This will initiate the user registration.
Alternatively, you can disable project selection (green) if you do not know the project, the
required project is missing or the list is empty (the project has not yet been created in our
SAP system (PH1) or you have not yet been assigned to the project in SharePoint).
4. Enter all the required information about the user:
Business partner details.
New user details.

User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
2 Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation DTS
Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation DTS (Kyano DTS) enables table-based migrations for various
SAP applications with fast data processing for standardized transformation scenarios such as
divestitures, mergers, harmonizations or technology upgrades within the existing IT landscape or
by moving systems to the cloud.
You can find further details in the Kyano DTS documentation.

=====PAGE 25=====
Version 25.09 SP00
Transformation Cockpit

=====PAGE 26=====
26
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
3 Transformation Cockpit
The Transformation Cockpit is an application for the execution of SAP® ERP system trans-
formations, which can be operated via the SAP® GUI.
3.1 Limitations
The following limitations apply to the migration of data between SAP® systems for the Trans-
formation Cockpit:
3.1.1 Backward Compatibility
Backward compatibility between the following releases is not supported:
S/4 →R3
The migration from an S/4 release to an R3 release cannot be supported due to the changed table
structure. In addition, there are limitations due to the reconversion of individual data types, e.g.
INT8 to INT4, and due to the length differences of some domains, e.g. Matnr 40 (18 characters).
6.0 →46c
The compression method of newer releases is not supported in older releases. However, the new
logic must be used, since the code page information must be observed during compression. The
way in which export files are compressed varies from release to release.

in the preview.
If transformation objects are assigned to a business object but are irrelevant according to
the blueprint file, they are not listed in the step Scenario import preview.

selection in the Scenario import preview step.

blueprint.
If you do not maintain any global selections in step 2, only the values from the imported
scenario are transferred.
If global selections are overwritten, the system displays a warning.
If the values of the global selection in step 2 are initial and the selection values of the scen-
ario import are not initial, they are not overwritten.

3.4.1.5.2 Conditions for the Entity Version
Scenario entities that meet the restriction criteria for the scenario parameters TGT_
S4CORE_VERSN, TGT_SAP_APPL_VERSN and SCENARIO_TYPE are classified as rel-
evant.
Global import rules that meet the restriction criteria for the scenario parameters TGT_
S4CORE_VERSN, TGT_SAP_APPL_VERSN, SCENARIO_TYPE and SC_MANDATORY
are classified as relevant.
Global export rules that meet the restriction criteria for the scenario parameters TGT_
S4CORE_VERSN, TGT_SAP_APPL_VERSN and SCENARIO_TYPE are classified as rel-
evant.
Entities without restriction criteria are classified as relevant.
The following entities are selected for the import by default:
Scenario parameters
Template runs
Number ranges
NOTE
No other runs are selected for the import by default.
NOTE
Unused number ranges are marked as Irrelevant.

The following object types are available, provided they are available in your source scen-

Objects: If objects already exist in the scenario into which you want to import the

Forerunners: If forerunners already exist in the scenario into which you want to

Global selections:
Overwrite for global selections: In overwrite mode, the global selections are

ted objects keep their connection to the imported global selections.
NOTE

the objects already contained in the scenario remain connected to the
global selections contained in the scenario.
Mappings: If mappings already exist in the scenario into which you want to import
the data, you can only overwrite them.
Global export/import/offset rules: If these rules already exist in the scenario into
which you want to import the data, you can only overwrite them.
Global functions: If global functions already exist in the scenario into which you want
to import the data, you can only overwrite them.
Global includes: can be imported if they do not yet exist in the target scenario. You
can overwrite existing global includes. It is always possible to rename a global
include. The new name must not yet exist in the target scenario.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter48

=====PAGE 49=====
NOTE
Uploaded global includes are linked to the same entities in the tar-
get scenario as in the file.
EXAMPLE
Global includes that are attached to a module in the file
are attached to the module with the same name in the
target scenario. If the module does not yet exist in the
target scenario, the module is created again.
Global includes that are not selected but exist in the target scen-
ario are added to the corresponding locations when the linked
entity is uploaded or created during the upload.
EXAMPLE
Global includes that are not uploaded but linked to a
module in the file are also linked to the module in the tar-
get scenario, provided that the module is created during
upload. This means that existing modules do not con-

modules by simply linking them together.
Runs: If runs already exist in the scenario into which you want to import the data,
you can only rename them.
NOTE

Rename and
enter a new name in the New identifier field.
To overwrite an object type, select the corresponding row and click
Over-
write.

how to start the table analysis.

ectory can be created, the system alternatively creates only one file under the specified file path.
The system then checks whether the file can be read per source system (per application server)
for each target system.
The directories and files created are cleaned up after the check. You will receive an error mes-
sage if the check fails.

3.5.1.8 Refreshing Table Statistics
Table statistics contain detailed information on the database and its objects. In order for the
optimizer to select and calculate the most efficient execution plan of an SQL query, information
about the tables and indexes involved in the SQL query must be available. The statistics include
the amount and distribution of the data in the database, the sizes of the tables involved, and the
selectivity of the existing indexes. System data is also available, for example I/O runtimes, the
size of the main memory, and the CPU speed. Histograms are another form of statistics. As
changes in the database occur all the time, it is important to refresh the statistics regularly so
that the optimizer can select and calculate the fastest execution plan.
This chapter describes how to refresh the table statistics.
Prerequisites
A scenario has been created.
The system connections of the scenario have already been defined.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter71

=====PAGE 72=====
Proceed as follows to refresh the table statistics:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click Systems.
2. Click
Refresh table statistics in the toolbar.
The view Transformation Cockpit - <scenario> - Change opens.
1. In the Systems to be refreshed field, specify the systems whose table statistics you want
to refresh.
NOTE
If you do not select a system, it is not possible to refresh the statistics.
2. In the Objects to be refreshed section, specify the objects you want to refresh.
NOTE
It is possible to refresh different tables. If you want to restrict your selection to
data objects, select the Migration tables option. You can now refresh all migra-
tion tables and inactive tables, or only include the data objects. To include data
objects, select the option Restrict to data objects and click Select from obj.
tree. Select which objects are to be included.
Moreover, you can refresh global selections, mappings, your own tables and
/SNP/ tables.
If you want to analyze individual tables, enable the Analyze any desired tables
option and enter the table names separated by commas.
3. In the Refresh if table change exceeds? section, you can specify the change percentage
that must be reached for a table to be refreshed.
NOTE
Tables that have already been refreshed and that only have changes below the
percentage you specified will not be refreshed.
4. Click
OK.
The table statistics are now being refreshed.
A message is displayed in the status bar stating that the table statistics refresh has been
scheduled in the background.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter72

=====PAGE 73=====
NOTE
Even if the Daemon is running, the table statistics are updated in the control system and
the source and target systems. This updates the statistics of the tables stored in the cus-
tomizing table /SNP/TE00TABREFT.
You can maintain the limit value for the deviation (percentage of the deviation between
the old state of the table and the new one) from which the update will be started via the
registry parameter TE.DAEMON.TAB_STAT_REF_THRESHOLD in the registry table
/SNP/CN00REGUV.
You can maintain the update interval at which the update of the table statistics is started
via the registry parameter TE.DAEMON.TAB_STAT_REF_INTERVAL_IN_MIN in the
registry table /SNP/CN00REGUV. The default value for the update interval is 30
minutes.

3.5.2 Data Objects
Data objects are used to group tables whose data records belong to a delineated unit. This unit
is mapped by a combination of these data records in an SAP® system.
Modules and data objects are displayed in alphabetical order in the tree.
Tables are usually sorted alphabetically according to their export sequence. You can
select an element in the tree and use the split button
Tables: by import sequence to
sort the tables according to their import sequence. If the tables are already sorted accord-
ing to their import sequence, you can use the split button
Tables: by export sequence
to re-sort the tables according to their export sequence.
The tooltip of a table icon
contains the alias of the corresponding table.
You can specify a selected node (module, object, table) as the root to restrict the view in
the data object tree. To do so, click
Selected node as root.
If the view is restricted, you can specify the parent node as the root of the view again. To
do so, select a node and click
Parent node as root.
You can hide inactive objects/tables and incompatible objects by clicking
Filter. The
following options are available: Inactive tables / Incompatible objects / Inactive objects.
If you want to show them again, click
Filter.
You can click the
Select layout split button to restructure the layout of an object. To
do so, select one of the following three options:
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter76

=====PAGE 77=====
Save layout: Saves the layout under the specified name.
Load layout: Displays a list of possible layouts that can be loaded.
Delete layouts: Displays a list of possible layouts that can be deleted.
NOTE
Incompatible objects are hidden by default.

User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter80

=====PAGE 81=====
NOTE
It is possible to specify predecessors for objects and forerunners.
These fields are also considered during the XML import. No problems are expected
when importing into a new scenario (i.e. when the scenario is created during the
import). However, when uploading (parts of) a scenario into an already existing scen-
ario, the following cases are possible:
The predecessor and successor are in the already existing scenario.
No relationships are changed between objects that already exist.
The predecessor and successor are both imported.
The existing relationship is adopted.
A predecessor or successor already exists. The missing one is imported. 
EXAMPLE
This case occurs when there is a predecessor -> successor rela-
tionship in the XML and the predecessor already exists in the scen-
ario, for example (i.e. the object V exists in the scenario but no
object N exists). In this case, the object N is imported and entered
as the successor of the already existing V (the reverse is also true).
At least one object already exists and is uploaded anyway (i.e. the new object
is renamed during the upload).
EXAMPLE
This case occurs when V and N both exist, and N is uploaded again
as N1. The relationship V -> N1 is created.
Note that any existing relationship is not considered in the already exist-
ing scenario.
EXAMPLE
In the scenario, the relationship V -> N already exists. In the
XML file, the objects V and N exist, but without a relationship.
If you upload N as N1, you might assume that this also cre-
ates the relationship V -> N1 (and that the reverse is also
true). However, this is not the case.

Save.

3.5.2.9 Business Objects
A business object describes an entity in the Transformation Cockpit. It is used to link data
objects in the Transformation Cockpit with functional aspects in an SAP system.
The business objects themselves as well as the links to data objects are delivered as part of the
Transformation Content. This information is used to apply the correct scope when using the SNP
scenario configurator to create a project scenario.
NOTE
You can use the Business objects tab in the Transformation Cockpit to see which
data objects are part of the corresponding scenario.

3.5.2.14 Lock Concepts for Objects
To ensure that only one person makes changes within an object, such as changes to tables,
rules or events, the Transformation Cockpit has a lock concept.
While you are making changes to an object or subobject, such as a table, rule or event, the
object is locked.
If another user tries to make changes to this object or its elements, they receive a message in
the status bar. The message contains the object concerned, a lock flag and the user who is cur-
rently editing the object.
NOTE
An object lock does not have any effect on global export rules, global import rules with
coding, global import rules with offset or global selections.

3. Right-click one of the selected objects.

The selected objects and tables have been activated/deactivated.

3.5.2.18 Mass Maintenance
This function is used for the mass maintenance of tables of a data object. The mass main-
tenance function is aimed at experienced users.
NOTE
Enter a number in the Import sequence column to define the sequence in which the
tables are imported. Tables with a lower value are processed earlier. Tables with a
higher value are processed later. The default value is 10. You can use values
between 1–9999.
The tables are always processed at the same level. Start tables, i.e., tables without a
parent table but with multiple child tables, are processed according to the sequence.
Child tables are processed depending on the sequence of all their sibling tables.
However, this only applies to tables with the same start table.
NOTE
In mass maintenance, you can use the
Change cell values button. The button offers
all the functions of the standard value help. You can use the keyboard shortcut for mass
selection (Ctrl+Y) to select several cells within a column. These cells are adjusted after
you select the desired value in the value help. Only selected and filtered cells/columns
are changed. If you have not selected any cells or cells without value help, clicking the
button has no effect.
Special features of the button compared to standard value help:
The button also works for checkboxes that normally have no value help. You can select
an entire column by clicking the column name. By clicking the button you can now
change all values in this column. Clicking the value help does not affect the selection of
an entire column. In combination, you can therefore set an entire column including
checkboxes to set/not set by clicking
Change cell values.

3.5.2.20 Syntax Check Export/Import
The syntax check allows you to check the rules, code assignment of mappings and system
restrictions for the export and import.
The following rules apply to the syntax check:
The syntax check is always started at the selected level (scenario, module, object, table,
data definition, event or rule). When starting the syntax check at the scenario level, all act-
ive and compatible objects in the scenario are taken into account; at the module level, all
active and compatible objects in the module are taken into account.
If an object is inactive, a superordinate object won’t take it into account during the syntax
check. However, the syntax check can be run directly on inactive objects.
If the syntax check runs on a table, only the table is checked. Child tables are not taken
into account.
Each local export event and data definition can only exist once due to system restrictions.
Each local import event, field rule and data definition can only exist once due to system
restrictions.
Each local forerunner event and data definition can only exist once due to system restric-
tions.

3.5.2.22 Rules
This chapter provides you with all the necessary information on how to use rules.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter111

=====PAGE 112=====
NOTE
Events, rules and field rules can exist multiple times and can have a system restriction.
3.5.2.22.1 Calling Rules Manually
All rules created in the Transformation Cockpit can be called manually in the respective context.
The generated call of events, field rules and global rules remains unaffected and continues to be
executed. With the additional call, it is possible, for example, to call events that are only called at
the beginning of a table at a later point in time.
NOTE
Context dependence
Rules that are only available in a certain context can only be called within this con-
text.
Possible: Call of the event Before data record processing (export) in the event After
data record processing (export) of the same table.
Not possible: Call of events or rules from other tables or objects as well as call of
object events out of a table or vice versa.

3.5.2.22.1.2 Calling Rules
All rules are forms that can be called by means of PERFORM. Any interface parameters must be
supplied as specified. If additional parameters have been defined, you can view them in the
respective rule and use them to call the rules.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter113

=====PAGE 114=====
EXAMPLE
Calling the event Before data record processing (export)
DATA lt_mara TYPE TABLE OF mara.
DATA lv_skip TYPE flag.
FIELD-SYMBOLS <ls_mara> TYPE mara.
"Call event Before data record processing for each record
LOOP AT lt_mara ASSIGNING <ls_mara>.
PERFORM _bef_row_sel
CHANGING
<ls_mara>
lv_skip.
IF lv_skip = 'X'.
DELETE lt_mara.
ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.

3.5.2.22.2.1 Tips on How to Use the Code Editor
Use the ABAP® key word help to obtain information and examples on key words. To do
this, position the cursor on a key word and press F1.
Use the auto-complete function to improve and accelerate the coding process. Begin by
entering the code; then press Ctrl+space bar to complete the element.
You can use the auto-complete function with the following elements:
TE environment variables
PERFORM statements in global functions, global export rules and global import
rules, depending on the context of the rule that is currently being edited (e.g. if it is
an import/export rule itself)
Your own data declarations/your own signatures
Global data declarations in the scope (e.g. table data declarations in table events)
Global type declarations (e.g. mapping types)
If you insert an API call and double-click it, the documentation on the API call opens if
available.

API_LOCK
Use API_LOCK to request any locks you want. Locks can be required if parallelization is
high and scenarios are running simultaneously in order to ensure that the transformation
or rule base works correctly.
Details
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter119

=====PAGE 120=====
When using API_LOCK, exclusive write locks are set so that multiple locks do not need to
be unlocked multiple times. However, requesting multiple locks in the same process is pos-
sible in contrast to the default behavior (sy-subrc = 0).
Automatic Unlocking
Because locks can only be released after successful processing (COMMIT) in most use
cases, yet no rule base can be executed at this point in time, all locks are automatically
released at the following points in time:
After completing the Scout
After completing the Direct Reader
After each package (export, import, forerunner)
Parameter
Parameter
Type
Value
iv_argument
ANY (internal: /SNP/TE0X_API_LOCK_ARGUMENT)
Any lock argument

API_MAPPING_ADD
You can use API_MAPPING_ADD to add new entries to mappings at runtime that were
not yet known before the execution. The entries added via API are marked as “auto-
matically added”. A table and/or object reference is also saved.
Prerequisites
The mapping is available and has been generated.
Interaction with API_MAPPING_SET
If API_MAPPING_ADD is executed multiple times for the same source value, a ter-
mination occurs when saving to the database. This prevents mappings from accidentally
being overwritten by processes running in parallel. This is usually useful because multiple
target values cannot exist for a single source value. If you want to overwrite the values,
use API_MAPPING_SET.
For a mapping, use either API_MAPPING_ADD or API_MAPPING_SET. Do not use both
at the same time. Otherwise, deadlocks can occur on the database if the same values are
processed by a process with API_MAPPING_ADD and by another process with API_
MAPPING_SET.

API_NRIV_STRATEGY_GET
Use API_NRIV_STRATEGY_GET to retrieve the strategy for a specific number range
object.
If you expect the strategy Difference calculation, set the parameter iv_value_old. API_
NRIV_STRATEGY_GET will then check if the value is included in the interval that is
allowed for the selected number range object. If the value is not included in the given inter-
val, the strategy Increment will be returned, even though Difference calculation has been
set. The strategy that is output by the API call is the technical name of the strategy as
described in the section Definition of the Strategies.
Prerequisites

maintained if necessary.

API_NUMBER_GET_NEXT
Use API_NUMBER_GET_NEXT to create a new number from a number range. The first
step is to calculate a new number using the NRIV offset definition and the old number.
If no more reserved numbers are available in the definition or if no definition exists, the
new number is generated using the function module NUMBER_GET_NEXT.
In addition to the new value, API_NUMBER_GET_NEXT also returns the strategy (incre-
ment, difference calculation, inactive, 1:1 transfer).
The strategy can differ from the one set in the Transformation Cockpit if the specified
strategy could not be used, during difference calculation or for a new number outside the
reserved area, for example.
Prerequisites
You can always use the API call if you want to create a new number from a number range.
If you want to calculate the new number from a reserved number range, you should per-
form the NRIV backup in SNP Transformation Cockpit regularly and over a longer period
of time. In addition, the number range level in the target system must be incremented and
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter136

=====PAGE 137=====
the NRIV offset definition loaded before the import using the program /SNP/TE01_NRIV_
OFFSET_UPDATE.

3.5.2.23 Tables
This chapter provides information on working with tables.
3.5.2.23.1 Settings
The Settings tab contains the relevant settings for the currently selected table.
Table
Displays the table name and label of the currently selected table.
Table alias
Aliases are used to uniquely identify tables of the same name within an object.
Initial assignment of aliases for tables:
When creating tables, unique aliases are automatically assigned within the object. The pat-
tern for generated aliases is the table name and (optionally) a number beginning with "2".
Tables are assigned the lowest alias that has not yet been set.
Manual assignment:
Aliases can be overwritten manually. If you change them at a later point, they must be
unique within the object.
The length of the alias is limited to 16 characters.
Use:
Table aliases are used to uniquely identify the tables during code generation, in free SQL
and when debugging exports.
Syntax check:
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter157

=====PAGE 158=====
The syntax check checks the uniqueness of each alias in relation to its selection tables.
Table status
This function allows you to specify the status of the table.
You can choose between A (active) and I (inactive).
Categories
Here you can specify one or more categories to enable or disable tables based on them.
NOTE
You can enter multiple categories separated by commas.
Commas are not allowed in the first or last position.
Consecutive commas are not allowed.
The permitted characters are A–Z, 0–9, minus and underscore.
Spaces are only allowed before or after a comma.
Duplicate categories are not allowed.
A maximum of 30 characters is allowed for the name of the category.
3.5.2.23.2 Export
The Export tab contains the relevant settings for the currently selected table.
Table
Displays the table name and label of the currently selected table.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter158

=====PAGE 159=====
Export method
This function allows you to influence the processing of individual tables during the export.
The following methods are available:
SR Scout Reader (Standard)
In the Scout Reader procedure, tables are processed using FOR ALL ENTRIES
selections. Dependent tables can only be processed after the respective selection
tables have been processed.
The selection table can be processed either in the same or another block. The last
performed export of the selection table is always used for the selection. If changes
are made to the table extension or if the export rule base is adjusted, the selection
tables should be exported again before processing the dependent tables.
NOTE
Once the Scout has processed the first package, a reader process can
start processing it.
Special features of start tables
Start tables are processed in two steps. In the first step (Scout), the keys to be
selected are gathered, taking into consideration the selections or the free
SQL. In the second step (Reader), the previously created packages with the
keys to be exported are selected and exported, and the packages for depend-
ent tables are saved.
The Scout is performed automatically with no more than one process per
table; the Reader can work with any number of processes. The Scout phase of
the start tables takes place before processing dependent tables.
Prioritization of work packages in export
Processing start tables: Scout or Direct Reader (tables with the export
method DR are ALWAYS start tables).
Packages of dependent tables and packages of start tables where the
Scout is already complete.
Packages of start tables where the Scout procedure is not yet complete.
Start tables, packages of dependent tables and packages of completely
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter159

=====PAGE 160=====
scouted tables are processed first. Only if there are no more pro-
cessable packages, those of an incomplete Scout are processed.
Effects on the transformation
The complete/processed records are now displayed before the Scout is com-
pleted. The total number grows continuously until all sentences have been
scouted. At the same time, the number of processed records increases if read-
ing has already begun.
What happens if an error occurs?
If a scout process terminates, no further packages of this table are processed
by Reader processes. A restart resets the complete progress (Scout and writ-
ten export files) and processing starts again.
DR Direct Reader
In the Direct Reader procedure, table connections are mapped via INNER JOINS. A
table (dependent and start table) is processed with exactly one statement.
Packages for dependent tables are only written if dependent tables exist that are not
processed using the Direct Reader. The actual export (files) is identical to an export
using the Scout Reader procedure.
A dependent table in direct reader mode can be processed independently of the
status of the selection table because its exported records are not required for its
own selection.
NOTE
Tables that use Direct Reader are always executed with only one pro-
cess, even if several processes are defined in the block. If you cancel the
export, the previous export progress is lost and the table is automatically
re-exported after a restart.
Switching Between the Export Methods
It is possible to change the export method at any time, but stored free SQL
must be adjusted in dependent tables. This is necessary because selection
tables (FOR ALL ENTRIES) are no longer available – as described above.
The export method is copied to the transformation table when creating it.
Changes to tables in data objects are therefore not transferred to already
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter160

=====PAGE 161=====
created or newly started blocks. This behavior is based on the fact that dif-
ferent programs are generated depending on the export method. Therefore,
already written files and FAE packages must be reset after switching the
method.
When the programs are generated (i.e. when starting the block), the export
method of the table in the data objects must correspond to the export method
of the transformation table. An error message appears if this is not the case.
Limitations and Warnings
Direct Reader:
It is not possible to use concatenated (complex) field connections when using
JOINS. This limitation applies to all direct and indirect table relationships.
If you switch to the Direct Reader method and there is a violation at the time of
the switch, the system issues a message.
If you perform a valid switch using the Direct Reader method, and sub-
sequently create complex connections in an indirect table relationship, errors
occur in the syntax check.
Export code that changes fields which are used to select the independent
tables; it can technically be used, but this is not recommended if the depend-
ent table is exported using the Direct Reader method. Changed fields are
ignored in this case due to the usage of JOINS and treated as if there were no
export code.
Contrary to the Scout Reader procedure, processes that were processed
using the Direct Reader and aborted cannot continue to run seamlessly after a
restart, but have to be completely reprocessed. This limitation also applies to
the Scout of the start tables.
NOTE
The Direct Reader can behave differently (performance) in dif-
ferent database systems and hierarchy levels (strong).
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter161

=====PAGE 162=====
DKP disabled
DKP (duplicate key prevention) is a function for preventing duplicate keys during the
import. The reason for duplicate keys is that certain dependent tables are processed as
packages.
DKP becomes active (on the dependent table) if not all key fields of the selection table are
used for the connection.
EXAMPLE
A field in the table extension is used instead of a key field.
Only one field of several key fields is used.
If there are multiple key fields and not all fields are linked, then DKP is also disabled if, for
the non-linked fields, there are field selections with just one unique value.
EXAMPLE
MARC
MARA
MARC and MARA have MATNR and WERKS as key fields. A
connection via MATNR would require DKP. However, if a
unique field selection is assigned to WERKS, e.g. WERKS =
'1000', DKP is not deactivated.
DKP avoids duplicate keys during the export. However, it causes significantly longer
runtimes due to the missing parallelization. Tables with active DKP are only ever pro-
cessed by one process, even if more processes have been specified for the execution.
You can disable DKP if you are sure that no duplicates will occur, or if you accept that you
might need to import using INSERT_ADK.
Disabled DKP is issued as a warning in the syntax check if required.
In general, next to the setting, you can see whether DKP is necessary.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter162

=====PAGE 163=====
Stick to the same process
This function ensures that the complete processing of the table, including all events and
rules, is performed within one process when the table is processed in the export. If a table
is processed using this function, it cannot be stopped. If an error occurs during pro-
cessing, the table must be reset before restarting it.
Selection mode
Choose the selection mode:
F: Field selection
S: Free selection (SQL) for entering complex SQL statements in SQL expert mode
N: Native SQL for native SQL statements
NOTE
The selection mode N (Native SQL) is not available via the F4 help. If you want to
write a statement in native SQL, you must manually set the selection mode N and
save.
Ignore redirect
If you enable this option, a proxy table is generated. It is a local table that references an
object.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter163

=====PAGE 164=====
NOTE
This proxy table is generated by default in the import if it is an SAP® S/4HANA
table.
Blocking factor (FAE)
Specification of the max. split factor for FOR ALL ENTRIES SQL statements
You can use this parameter to specify the number of records of the selection package for
which an actual select is executed on the database.
Default values:
Transparent tables: 10
Pool/cluster tables: 5
This parameter value is generated using a hint to the SQL statement in order to optimize it
accordingly.
NOTE
Decrease the blocking factor in the case of memory problems and increase it in
the case of performance problems. We recommend a maximum change of
1,000. However, an adjustment of up to a maximum of 250 is usually reas-
onable.
EXAMPLE
If the blocking factor is 10, for an FAE select with 50 records in the selection
table (ABAP®), 5 dedicated selects are actually executed on the database and
the result set is merged before it is transferred to the application server. This
artificial subdivision is not visible in the ABAP® debugger.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter164

=====PAGE 165=====
FAE package size (records)
Specification of the segmentation size of a package into sub-packages
Reducing the FAE package size leads to several smaller selections, thus helping to
reduce the memory requirements during the export. For most tables, this parameter does
not affect the package size and the content of the export files. Tables with a dynamic
record size are an exception. Here, the package size in MB directly determines the file
size. However, a check to verify whether a file is full is always performed after a certain
number of records, which is limited by the FAE package size.
For tables with a static record width, i.e. the majority of tables, the default value is 0. This
corresponds to the package size of the selection table or, for start tables, the package size
of the table itself. For tables with a dynamic record width, i.e. with fields of STRING-like
data types, the default value is 10.
NOTE
Reduce the FAE package size if memory problems occur when selecting data
in dependent tables, cluster tables or tables with a dynamic record width, and if
you cannot resolve these issues by changing the package size to a reasonable
number. The FAE package size of a dependent table behaves similarly to the
package size of the parent table without having to reexport the parent table
with a small package size. The export files created after the reduction are
saved with the new package size specified in the scenario or on the table.
Package size (records/MB)
You can specify the package size for each table.
If no package size is specified for a table (field is empty), the package size of the
scenario is used.
If the value is 0, all records are transferred to a package.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter165

=====PAGE 166=====
NOTE
The package size set in the scenario can be overridden on the table. You can
specify the value in records or MB. If the value entered includes MB, the num-
ber is interpreted as a megabyte value. If the value includes only numbers,
they are specified as records. The override can be in both directions. You can
select larger or smaller packages than defined in the scenario.
Parallel hint (Oracle)
Specification of the parallelization number for SQL statements on Oracle
This value is generated using a hint to the SQL statement. This hint is only used on Oracle
database systems and only
applies to start tables and tables set to DR. The default value is 4.

3.5.2.23.2.4 Native SQL
You can create SQL statements in native SQL. This can be necessary if you use many subse-
lects, for example. Subselects are limited to 10 in free SQL.
Limitations and prerequisites for native SQL
The selection mode can only be used for start tables; dependent tables are not supported.
Native SQL is only supported as of SAP® Basis Release >= 620.
You must write the entire statement yourself. No automatic conversion takes place as is
the case when switching to free SQL.
Placeholders are not supported (the usual placeholders from free SQL are not supported
for global selections, for example).
The mode is not displayed in the F4 help.
The syntax of the statement is not checked.
Proceed as follows to use native SQL for a selection:
1. Click
Data objects in the left-hand navigation bar.
2. Double-click a table.
3. Go to the Export tab.
4. In the selection mode field, enter the mode N.
NOTE
The mode N is not available in the F4 help.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter174

=====PAGE 175=====
5. Press Enter.
NOTE
Switching to Expert mode can lead to a loss of information.
6. Confirm the prompt with Yes.
7. Assign a title.
8. Enter an SQL statement.
9. Click
Save.
The SQL statement has been created.
Examples of Native SQL
Export method SR (select only key fields):
SELECT MANDT, MATNR FROM MARA
Export method DR (select all fields in the table):
SELECT MANDT, MATNR, [remaining fields of MARA] FROM MARA

NOTE
Scope
The global rule can be used for multiple data elements. The scope determines
whether a global rule is applied to a table field. If a table field corresponds to
the type of scope, the global rule is applied to this table field. This applies to all
tables of this type. A field rule overrides this behavior of global rules.
NOTE
Empty scope of global rules
Main use case: Creating incomplete rules that contain code and implementing
them at a later date.
The scope of global rules can be empty. However, if the scope is empty, you
cannot maintain field usages for these global rules. The rules are not taken into
account during execution and for the display in the data objects, since no tech-
nical assignment is possible.
You can edit rules without scope as usual. This means that you can maintain
and check code and also create parameters that you can use in the code.
However, the cross-reference list does not provide any results since no tech-
nical assignment is possible.
A row is added to the table in the Scope section.
The element type Domain is preset. The element types domain, data element and table
field are available.
If you select the table field element type, use the value help to select the table first. A win-
dow for selecting the table field appears. The element name field then displays a com-
posite name consisting of the table and the table field (e.g. MARA-MATNR).

that only exist in the differing target table. The fields remain empty if they
are not filled through a field rule or event, and if no corresponding table
extension has been defined for the export.
Import Sequence
Enter a number in the Import sequence column to define the sequence in which the tables
are imported. Tables with a lower value are processed earlier. Tables with a higher value
are processed later. The default value is 10. You can use values between 1–9999.
The tables are always processed at the same level. Start tables, i.e., tables without a par-
ent table but with multiple child tables, are processed according to the sequence. Child
tables are processed depending on the sequence of all their sibling tables. However, this
only applies to tables with the same start table.
Stick to the same process
This function ensures that the complete processing of the table, including all events and
rules, is performed within one process when the table is processed in the import. If a table
is processed using this function, it cannot be stopped. If an error occurs during pro-
cessing, the table must be reset before restarting it.
NOTE
For further information, refer to the Modes and Options chapter.

3.5.2.23.5 Table Extension
If you need additional fields in a table, you can use the table extension feature to create new
fields. For each added field, you can define the following:
Name
Data type
Number of digits
Decimal places
In addition, the table extension feature allows you to fill the fields based on a selection table. To
do this, specify the desired field from a selection table as the default value in the table extension.
During the export, this field is then filled with the values from the specified field in the selection
table. Use the value help to select the fields. Alternatively, you can specify an alias field name.
All other default values must be specified as follows: 'abc' or '123' or '100-100'.
NOTE
In addition to the export, the fields of the table extension are also available for the import
(target structures/target tables) (TARGET_XXX, TAB_TARGET_XXX).
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter194

=====PAGE 195=====
NOTE
When filling field values from selection tables (ALIAS-FIELD NAME), only simple
comparison operators are allowed in free SQL (EQ or =). Nesting several conditions
with the operator OR is not allowed. The exact connection is required so that it is pos-
sible to clearly assign the values from selection tables. When using the operator OR
or comparison operators such as GT or LE, this clear assignment is not possible. In
the best case, it leads to a process termination, but in the worst case, it leads to incor-
rectly transferred field values.

NOTE
Technically, there is an n:1 relationship between the selection table and
the dependent table. This means that a data record in the selection table
can reference multiple data records in the dependent table. The value in
the field extension that is filled from the selection table assumes any one
of these n values. This causes an error when you try to save the value.
Technically, it is an n:1 relationship, but de facto, it is a 1:1 relationship. If
you ignore the check, the assumed value can be saved.

3.5.2.23.9 Virtual Tables
You have the option to create virtual tables on your control system. You can import data from
non-SAP® systems into these tables, and import them into real SAP® tables in the target sys-
tem. For the import into the target system, the import rule base you created is used. The data
from the non-SAP® system must be available as a CSV file. The first row is interpreted as the
header, the following rows as data.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter201

=====PAGE 202=====
3.5.2.23.9.1 Notes on Virtual Tables
Each field in the virtual table initially has the type character 50, which can be changed if neces-
sary.
After the upload, you can use the export log of the table to view when and from which file data
was uploaded and how many data records were uploaded. The structure of the log corresponds
to that of regular tables after an export.
No export syntax check is performed on virtual tables, because neither selections nor the export
rule base apply to them.
Virtual Tables
must begin with $.
cannot be used as root nodes for other tables.
can only be created at the top level of the object.
must have a differing target table, otherwise they cannot be imported.
do not have an export rule base since they can only be uploaded, not exported.
cannot be used in export blocks.
are ignored in single executions of objects.
cannot be located under other tables in the object detail dialog of the mass maintenance.

3.5.2.23.10 Table Pools and Table Clusters
Tables like RFBLG, KOCLU (cluster) and ATAB (pool) can be created directly in the Trans-
formation Cockpit. You can also read and write in these tables directly.
NOTE
Release differences between source and target systems, different structures in the data-
base and non-Unicode/Unicode can lead to problems.
Information on Table Pools and Table Clusters
Table pools (pools) and table clusters (clusters) are special table types in the ABAP® Dictionary.
You can store data of multiple different tables in a table pool or table cluster. The tables
assigned to a table pool or table cluster are called pool tables or cluster tables.
When importing cluster tables (such as BSEG) with several processes as well as when import-
ing several tables of the same cluster (such as BSEG or BSET) simultaneously, process ter-
minations can occur. In this case, the SAP® database interface tried to insert two records of the
cluster table (BSEG) that belong to the same entry in the cluster (e.g. RFBLG) at the same time.
You can avoid this by setting the table lock for the relevant table (see chapter Properties of Entit-
ies). If you want to import several cluster tables in the same block for one cluster, you can also
restrict the maximum number of processes of the block to 1.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter203

=====PAGE 204=====
However, with this procedure, the table(s) are not processed in parallel. It often makes more
sense to perform the import with several processes, even if terminations occur. Afterwards, you
can restart the tables. During the second run, terminations should not occur.
NOTE
Using the cluster (e.g. RFBLG) or the pool (e.g. ATAB) directly is only useful in excep-
tional cases. Usually, logical tables (cluster tables such as BSEG or pool tables such
as T001E) should be used in the scenario and not the pools/clusters themselves.
WARNING
If clusters such as RFBLG are used directly, it is not useful if the included cluster
tables (such as BSEG) are also included in the scenario. This can lead to irreversible
database inconsistencies.
For further information, click here.

3.5.2.23.13 Clarification on Tables
This chapter provides information about selection tables and dependent tables. Tables have
dependencies that restrict the selection criteria for dependent tables. Tables are linked via table
connections (also across objects).
3.5.2.23.13.1 Selection Tables
A selection table (also header table) restricts dependent tables according to specific criteria.
Table connections for selection tables are also possible across objects, i.e. they can also be
included in other data objects of the same scenario.
3.5.2.23.13.2 Dependent Tables
Dependent tables (also child tables) are displayed below the selection table. Dependent tables
can be created via the mass maintenance of the data object. You can create connections across
objects via the context menu (right-click the table > Link to selection table).

Are the values of the fields FROMNUMBER and
TONUMBER of the NRIV identical on all the specified source
systems and the target system? This is a prerequisite for
using the strategy 1:1.
Update NRIV
The update is based on the saved number range objects and their
settings.
Only the number ranges that use the strategies Difference
calculation and 1:1 are incremented; other strategies are not
taken into account.
For the strategy Difference calculation, the specified source
systems are used to calculate the offsets of the number
ranges.
You can maintain the factors buffer in % (NRIV offset factor)

Function
and fixed buffer (safety factor) directly in the number range.
For the strategy 1:1, the highest number range level of the
source system is used as long as it is higher than in the tar-
get system, and as long as the values of the fields
FROMNUMBER and TONUMBER match.
Irrelevant number range objects are not taken into account.

3.5.3.2 Saving NRIV Tables
Use this function to save the current number range levels that are stored in the NRIV tables of
the source and target systems on the control system before the project starts.
This allows you to determine the current number range levels during the project.
You can find the saved data in the table /SNP/TE00NRIV of the corresponding control system.
If you want to use the Difference procedure, it is useful to save the NRIV multiple times over a
certain period of time. This allows a better and more precise determination of the growth of the
number range for later calculation.
Prerequisites
Source and target systems have been specified.
Proceed as follows:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click
Number ranges.
2. In the toolbar, click
Save NRIV.
The system saves the data.
Once the data has been successfully saved, the message NRIV successfully saved is dis-
played in the status bar.

3.5.3.3.1 General checks
Does the number range exist on the target system?
Is the number range on the target system an external number range? Only the strategy
Inactive is allowed for external number ranges.
3.5.3.3.2 Checks for the strategy Difference calculation
Have source systems been maintained for the number range? You must specify source
systems for the strategy Difference calculation.
Is there an overflow of the number range? The software checks whether the number
ranges of all specified source systems fit into the free area of the number range on the tar-
get system or whether an overflow of the number range occurs.
Have the number range objects for the specified source systems and the target system
been saved? The backup is necessary.
3.5.3.3.3 Checks for the strategy 1:1
Have source systems been maintained for the number range? You must specify source
systems for the strategy 1:1.
Does the number range exist on the specified source system?
Is there an overflow of the number range? The system checks whether the highest number
level of the number ranges of the source systems fits into the number range area of the tar-
get system or whether there is an overflow of the number range.
Are the values of the fields FROMNUMBER and TONUMBER of the NRIV identical on all
the specified source systems and the target system? This is a prerequisite for using the
strategy 1:1.

3.5.3.4 Updating an NRIV
The NRIV update function allows you to increment the number ranges in the target system and
reserve numbers for the migration.
During the update, the strategies and settings such as the buffer of the selected number range
are transferred to the target system.
The transferred number range strategies are used to determine the new value when calling the
API call api_number_get_next.
If the number range strategy has not been transferred, the API call cannot be used. In this case,
the system issues a message.

WARNING

If a lower release is used as the control system for Transformation Cockpit, the fol-
lowing functions are not supported for the SNP Transformation Cockpit:

Creation of global selections for a domain with the data type dec-
float16/decfloat34
Creation of mappings for a domain with the data type decfloat16/decfloat34
Creation of own table definitions with a data element of data types dec-
float16/decfloat34
The export/import as well as the syntax check of a table with a field that uses one of
the two data types are possible without problems.
You can use a global selection to specify values for exactly one table field. This field is used to
identify the data records of the table that are to be selected and changed.
The global selection is reusable. This means that it can be applied to other fields in other tables
in the same scenario.
In the Selections tab, the global selections created in the scenario are listed in the table. The fol-
lowing information is available in the table: 
Column
Explanation

The Mode column shows the read mode you specified while creating the global
selection. For further information on the read mode, see the Creating Global Selec-
tions chapter.

The Amount column shows how many values have been maintained for the global
selection.

User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter220

=====PAGE 221=====
NOTE
If you create a new global selection in dialog, you cannot use values exceeding
45 characters.
If you create a new global selection using an API (API_SELECTION_ADD),
you cannot use values exceeding 50 characters. More than 50 characters are
truncated in the table field during execution.
If you want to use longer domains for a select, create a separate table that can
be used in the rule base or in free SQL to select the data.
Proceed as follows to create a global selection:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click Global.
2. Go to the Selections tab.
3. Click
Add global selection.
4. Assign a unique ID.
5. Assign a title.
6. Optional: Assign categories.
7. Specify the read mode you want to use:
Cached Read: All values are loaded during the first call and kept in the memory
(fast but memory-intensive).
Single Read: Values are never kept in the memory, but rather only collected on
request (slow but memory-efficient).
8. If you want to allow range values, fuzzy values and exclusions, enable the Use complex
selections option.
NOTE
When using complex selections, you can only use the Cached Read mode.
NOTE
If you do not include complex selections, you can only maintain single values.
Input screens without complex selections only have a column that has the type
of the specified domain. For complex selections, a table with the columns of a
select option is created.
9. Confirm the prompt.
10. Enable the Optimize selection for parallel writing option in order to avoid lock conflicts on
the database level if different processes write the same selection values.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter221

=====PAGE 222=====
NOTE
If the option is inactive, the process ID remains empty when writing the values.
Selection values can only be written once into the table. Conflicts can arise. If
the option is active, the process ID is filled when writing the values. Different
processes can write the same value at the same time without risking any con-
flicts. However, it is possible that selection values are written several times into
the generated table. This can increase memory requirements in the database.
NOTE
The option does not have any influence on the function of the global selection
and API calls. The usage of global selections works as usual.
NOTE
You can enable the option during already started transformations without data
loss. To apply the option, you must start a new execution or stop and restart an
execution that has already been started.
11. Optional: Enable the Released option if you want to publish the selection for external main-
tenance and thus make it visible and editable.
12. Enter a domain.
13. Enter the values for the global selection per system.
14. Click Save & close.
The global selection has been created.
NOTE
You can also use the global selection in the target system to select data from the export.

condition must be met so that the record is exported. If only one field per table
is selected, the corresponding selection is always linked as a field selection.
WARNING

float34 were introduced for decimal floating point numbers.

following functions are not supported for the SNP Transformation Cockpit:
Creation of field selections on a field with the data type dec-
float16/decfloat34
Creation of global selections for a domain with the data type dec-
float16/decfloat34
Creation of mappings for a domain with the data type dec-
float16/decfloat34
Creation of own table definitions with a data element of data types dec-
float16/decfloat34
The export/import as well as the syntax check of a table with a field that uses
one of the two data types are possible without problems.

3.5.4.5.12 Checking and Generating Global Selections Manually
For global selections, you can check structural differences and generate tables manually in the
satellite system. It is recommended to use both functions in combination: first you perform the
check and then the generation.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter234

=====PAGE 235=====
NOTE
You can use the Structural differences function to check whether the respect-
ive definition in the control system corresponds to the generated table in the
satellite system. This indicates whether the table would be regenerated in case
of an execution (export or import). Differences are displayed if new manual val-
ues have been created for the selection since the last generation or if the table
has been generated by an execution (export or import). You can perform this
check for multiple or all selections at once.
The Generate table function enables a manual generation that allows you to
regenerate tables in the satellite system. In contrast to automated generation
(e.g. when starting an export or import), the corresponding table is regenerated
each time. This is especially useful if automated generation fails. Manual gen-
eration can save time during the actual transformation, because it is no longer
necessary to generate the tables during preparation.
WARNING
During manual generation, automatically added entries on the selec-
ted system are deleted from the table.

3.5.4.6 Mappings
Mapping is a technical term that describes, in the form of a table, how data fields are to be
changed. Each row of the table contains at least the source value and the target value.
You can use the source value to identify the data field whose value should be changed. The tar-
get value is the exact value that should be written to the identified data field.
Usage
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter239

=====PAGE 240=====
You can apply mappings in combination with field rules or global rules. It is also possible to
access mappings via API calls in events and forms.

3.5.4.6.5 Validating Mapping Tables in Rules
You have the option to validate mapping tables in rules.
The following checks are performed during this process:
Duplicate source values (1:N mappings)
Empty values
N:1 mappings (different source values for one target value) are issued as a warning
The system issues a maximum of 100 errors/warnings. Errors are issued and handled with pri-
ority.
NOTE
Only mappings that have been added in the Transformation Cockpit are validated. Map-
pings added in the Cockpit overwrite manually created mappings on the source/target
system.
Mapping tables can be validated as follows:
In the mapping rule by clicking
Validate
In the mapping rule by saving or clicking Save and close
If the validation fails, an error message that explains the error is displayed in the message area.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter247

=====PAGE 248=====
If you perform the validation using the
Validate button and the validation fails, the error mes-
sage is displayed in the message area of the mapping rule.
The Save and Save and close buttons result in the deletion of invalid mapping lines.
NOTE
Double-click the error message to jump to the erroneous line of the mapping rule. If the
line that the error message refers to is hidden by a filter, a corresponding message is dis-
played in the status bar when you try to jump to the erroneous line.

3.5.4.6.12 Checking and Generating Mappings Manually

has been generated by an execution (export or import). You can perform this
check for multiple or all mappings at once.
The Generate table function enables a manual generation that allows you to

3.5.4.7 Global Rules Export/Import
Global rules are the link between the table fields whose data is to be changed and the reusable
transformation modules such as mappings and forms. As opposed to a field rule that can only
affect a single table field, a global rule can apply to multiple fields in multiple tables from dif-
ferent data objects. To identify the table fields to which the global rule should be applied, you
can specify different search patterns for table fields, for their data elements and/or for their
domain.
The two types of global rules are global export rules and global import rules. Creating, editing
and deleting global rules does not differ between export and import rules. These processes are
therefore described in general terms.
NOTE
Global rules are not automatically applied to your own tables.
Create a field rule or enter the corresponding table field in the global rule.
3.5.4.7.1 Creating Global Rules
This function allows you to create a global rule for a domain, data element or table field. The rule
has an effect on all tables that correspond to this pattern.
Prerequisites
A scenario has been created.
The system landscape has been set up.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter259

=====PAGE 260=====
NOTE
Global rules must not overlap. For example, DOMA MATNR and DTEL MATNR are not
allowed in a single rule because the data element includes the domain. This would be
possible in two different rules because the more precise rule overwrites the more gen-
eral one in certain cases. However, if a field rule is defined, the field rule is used.
Proceed as follows to create a global rule:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click
Global.
2. Go to the Export rule or Import rule tab depending on the project phase you want to cre-
ate the rule for.
3. Click
Add rule.
The type field is predefined with Global rule with coding.
4. In the Scope area, click
Add.
NOTE
Scope
The global rule can be used for multiple data elements. The scope determines
whether a global rule is applied to a table field. If a table field corresponds to
the type of scope, the global rule is applied to this table field. This applies to all
tables of this type. A field rule overrides this behavior of global rules.
NOTE
Empty scope of global rules
Main use case: Creating incomplete rules that contain code and implementing
them at a later date.
The scope of global rules can be empty. However, if the scope is empty, you
cannot maintain field usages for these global rules. The rules are not taken into
account during execution and for the display in the data objects, since no tech-
nical assignment is possible.
You can edit rules without scope as usual. This means that you can maintain
and check code and also create parameters that you can use in the code.
However, the cross-reference list does not provide any results since no tech-
nical assignment is possible.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter260

=====PAGE 261=====

3.5.4.8 Offsets
Offsets are used for the following purpose:
Many database table fields are assigned general domains, such as CHAR90. Both simple and
concatenated key fields from other tables are partially stored in these fields (e.g. STXH-
TDNAME with MATNR domain and/or WERKS domain).
Since these contents must also be mapped taking the global rules into consideration, it is neces-
sary to define how the respective field is to be split.
Offset rules are used to split fields. Offset rules enable you to define the positions of key fields in
database fields.

3.5.4.8.4.1 General Information on Restricting Parameters
Parameters are considered incompatible for entities if at least one of the following conditions
applies:
In the restriction of the entity, the value of the global parameter is not included in the list of
values of the defined parameters.
The value of the parameter is not maintained in the restriction of the entity (empty). But the
global parameter has a non-initial value.
The global parameter has a value that is not contained in the list of allowed values.
In general, this is an invalid status that cannot be saved in the Global parameters
area.
In these specific cases, the entity that is using the parameter in its restriction is
always considered as incompatible to emphasize the underlying inconsistency.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter271

=====PAGE 272=====
NOTE
These restrictions ensure that the parameters are correctly coordinated, pre-
venting unintended behavior and inconsistencies.
3.5.4.8.5 Example of Using Offsets
The following chapter shows an example of using an offset when mapping values of the MATNR
domain.
Problem:
Depending on the content of other table fields, the TDNAME field of the STXH table is composed
of several domains.
To access the MATNR domain in the TDNAME field, an offset must therefore be defined.
1. Entering the scope:
The TDOBNAME data element is specified as the scope because this data element is loc-
ated behind the TDNAME field in the STXH table.
2. Defining parameters:
In the parameter definition, the following three values are required to determine the con-
ditions under which the offset should have an effect.
PARAM_TDOBJECT
PARAM_TDID
PARAM_SPRAS
The parameters represent the table fields of the STXH table whose values determine the
position of the MATNR domain in the TDNAME field.
3. Maintaining parameter usage:
The window displays all tables with their corresponding fields that were added to the scen-
ario and in which the data element selected in the scope is stored.
In this example, the STXH table and the TDNAME field are included. The previously cre-
ated parameters must now be filled with the corresponding fields from the table or with the
literals.
PARAM_TDOBJECT = TDOBJECT
PARAM_TDID = TDID
PARAM_TSPRAS = TSPRAS.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter272

=====PAGE 273=====
4.
Adding and maintaining segmentation:
You can use the segmentation to split the TDNAME field according to domains, depending
on the field contents of the parameters.
Parameters:
PARAM_TDOBJECT (corresponds to the TDOBJECT field in the example) =
MVKE
PARAM_TDID (corresponds to the TDID field in the example) = 0001
PARAM_TSPRAS (corresponds to the TSPRAS field in the example) = D
Segmentation:
Domain name: MATNR
Domain name: VKORG
If MATNR has 18 characters and VKORG has 4 characters, this means that the field TDNAME
consists of the domain MATNR from position 0 to 18 and of the domain VKORG from position 19
to 23.
NOTE
The Relative offset position field is used if gaps exist between the domains. In this
case, enter the length of the gap (number of characters).
This is the case only if the conditions of the parameters are met, i.e. if "MVKE" is in the
TDOBJECT field, "0001" in the TDID field, and "D" in the TDSPRAS field. You can define any
number of conditions to split the TDNAME field.
In this case, the offset would call a global rule on the MATNR domain in order to map the first 18
digits in the TDNAME field.
NOTE
The introduction of S/4HANA required to change the length of some domains. Thus
the domain MATNR no longer consists of 18 characters, but of 40. This change is
also taken into account for offsets.
Due to the differences in length, it had been necessary to create global import rules
for all used domains to ensure correct processing. The code of these rules also had
to include the line ev_value = iv_value, provided that no other rule base is
applied. This is no longer necessary. You must no longer create a global import rule.
Areas of an offset without an import rule are now transferred 1:1 automatically.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter273

=====PAGE 274=====
3.5.4.9 Events
Global events are events that you can define globally for each scenario. The scope allows you to
determine the objects (module/table/data object) to which the global event should be applied.
NOTE
If you do not specify a scope, the event has an effect on all objects in the scenario.
Global events are subject to the following restrictions:
The global event can only be created once per scenario (one for the export and one for the
import).
The event applies to all specified tables (e.g. module MM – all tables in this module).
The global event is executed after the event After package processing for each specified
table. It has an additional effect.

3.5.4.9.4.1 General Information on Restricting Parameters
Parameters are considered incompatible for entities if at least one of the following conditions
applies:
In the restriction of the entity, the value of the global parameter is not included in the list of
values of the defined parameters.
The value of the parameter is not maintained in the restriction of the entity (empty). But the
global parameter has a non-initial value.
The global parameter has a value that is not contained in the list of allowed values.
In general, this is an invalid status that cannot be saved in the Global parameters
area.
In these specific cases, the entity that is using the parameter in its restriction is
always considered as incompatible to emphasize the underlying inconsistency.
NOTE
These restrictions ensure that the parameters are correctly coordinated, pre-
venting unintended behavior and inconsistencies.

the two data types are possible without problems.

ario export/import.

fore, make sure that they are correctly used.
NOTE
Global rules automatically have an effect on your own tables if a data element has
been defined for the table field.

responding table field in the global rule.

3.5.6.1.3 Checking and Generating Individual Tables Manually
For individual tables, you can check structural differences and generate tables manually in the
satellite system. It is recommended to use both functions in combination: first you perform the
check and then the generation.
NOTE
You can use the Structural differences function to check whether the respect-
ive definition in the control system corresponds to the generated table in the
satellite system. This indicates whether the table would be regenerated in case
of an execution (export or import). In addition, you can display structural dif-
ferences. You can perform this check for multiple or all individual tables at
once.
The Generate table function enables a manual generation that allows you to
regenerate tables in the satellite system. In contrast to automated generation
(e.g. when starting an export or import), the corresponding table is regenerated
each time. This is especially useful if automated generation fails. Manual gen-
eration can save time during the actual transformation, because it is no longer
necessary to generate the tables during preparation.

3.5.6.1.4 Refreshing the Remote DDIC for Your Own Tables
You can use this function to add subsequently table and field information to the table analysis.
If you create or edit your own tables, these or the changes made do not yet exist in the system.
However, by including your own table in the table analysis, you can use it in the Transformation
Cockpit as if it already existed in the system. This allows the table to be added directly to a data
object, for example.
In an actual execution, the own table is then generated on the respective system and the data in
the table analysis then corresponds to the table in the satellite system.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter295

=====PAGE 296=====
If you download a scenario with your own tables and upload it elsewhere, the information cannot
be included in the table analysis of the new scenario automatically because system information
may not yet be available at this point.
Even after systems have been maintained, this information is not subsequently added, which
means that the table cannot be used in the scenario as described above. When you call the
detailed view, execute syntax checks or perform other actions, the system displays the message
that the table does not exist on system XY.
Using the function Refresh remote DDIC for own tables, the required information is sub-
sequently included in the table analysis.
NOTE
Execute the function whenever you have uploaded a scenario. Otherwise, errors are
issued when the syntax check is executed because the system does not know the
tables.
Proceed as follows to refresh the remote DDIC for own tables:

3.5.6.2 Parameters
In the Parameters tab, you have the option of creating and maintaining all the required para-
meters in a central location. You can then use the parameters globally in the rule base. Para-
meters are used, among other things, to control different events at various points in the rule
base when the same trigger is used.
3.5.6.2.1 Creating Parameters
This chapter describes how to create and delete a parameter.
Prerequisites
A scenario has been created.
Source and target systems are maintained in the scenario.
Proceed as follows to create a parameter: 
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/TC.
2. In the left-hand navigation bar, click Global.
3. Go to the Parameters tab.
4. Click
Add new parameter.
The window Create parameter for scenario <scenario name> opens.
4. Enter a Name for the new parameter.
5. Enter a Description for the parameter.
6. Click
OK.
A new row is created in the ALV grid with the desired name, the description, the data type
CHAR and the length 1.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter299

=====PAGE 300=====
NOTE
You can manually adjust the data type subsequently. The following data types
are available:
CHAR, DATS, DEC, INT1, INT2, INT4, LANG, NUMC, TIMS, STRG
You cannot use complex data types such as structures, references or table
types.
7. Optional: Specify a Category as additional information in order to categorize the new para-
meter.
8. To copy an already existing row, select the row and click
Copy parameter.
9. Enter a Name for the copied parameter.
10. Enter a Description for the copied parameter.
11. Click
OK to paste the copied row and to apply all the other information from the tem-
plate.
Like all parameters, you can use the parameter for the code of newly created global rules,
free SQL or global includes.
NOTE
When using code completion to complete the parameter, the code must be syn-
tactically correct.
You can use TE_PARAMETERS-XX' to access the values. XX corresponds to the pre-
viously defined name. The parameters are transferred when the scenario is uploaded or
downloaded. When you upload the scenario, the parameters can also be overwritten.
