3.5.7.5 Comparing Transformations at Object Level and Table Level
You can compare different transformations from one or more scenarios. This comparison can be
performed at the data object or table level. If the comparison takes place at the object level, the
runtimes of the selected objects are compared with each other / set in relation. If the comparison
takes place at the table level, the record counts and runtimes of the respective table are com-
pared with each other. The assignment is made via the table alias for each object.
If you want to compare several transformations, you must first define a leading transformation.
The remaining selected transformations are compared with its results.
Prerequisites
You have already performed several transformations.
Proceed as follows to compare transformations:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click
Transformation.
2. In the toolbar, click
Compare transformations.
The window Selection of data sources for comparison opens.
3. Use the split button to choose whether you want to display the table level or the object
level.
NOTE
You can also switch between the two display modes when the comparison has
been performed.
4. Click
Add new data source.
The Select area window opens.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter305

=====PAGE 306=====
5. Add a scenario as the data source.
6. Optional: Make further restrictions that are to be taken into account for the comparison.
NOTE
If you want to remove a data source, select it and click
Delete selected
data sources.
7. Add at least one additional data source.
NOTE
You must select at least two data sources for a comparison.
NOTE
You can also import data sources that you have previously exported. To do
this, click
Import data source and specify the path to the desired file.
8. Click
OK.
The comparison is performed and displayed in the Compare transformations window.
The following functions are available in the Compare transformations window:
Switch leading transformation: Define the transformation with which the other
selected transformations are to be compared.
Display table level / Display object level: Specify the perspective from which
you want to view the comparison.
Export data source: Select a data source that you want to export and save loc-
ally.
Import data source: Select a local data source for the import that is to be
included in the comparison.
NOTE
The data source to be imported must correspond to the correct level
(table level or object level).
NOTE

no longer be used.

User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter308

=====PAGE 309=====
Column
Description
tables left to be scouted (the selecting and storing of key records), and no
packages of completed Scouts exist that can be processed.
Processed records
Displays the number of data records written to files
Information on record counts:
Why have I processed fewer records than the total number of
records?
This can happen when the rule base skips data records AFTER
the selection (EV_SKIP). These data records are selected but not
written to files.
Why does the total number of records increase simultaneously
with the processed records, even though both procedures
(Scout/Reader) are performed successively?
This can happen when exporting cluster tables. The following pro-
cedure is based on the question above:
Table: REGUP
Cluster: REGUC
To simplify the example, we will assume that the package has
10,000 records.
The Scout reads keys with the package size 10,000 from
REGUC. The reason for this is that cluster access is quick
with the cluster key. If the keys of the REGUP entries were
scouted, this would lead to a full table scan of the cluster in
the read process (slow).
The reader reads data records from the table REGUP with
the scouted keys of the cluster REGUC. It should be noted
that the key of the cluster is more fuzzy than the key of the
table REGUP. (It can be seen in SE11; REGUP has the fol-
lowing additional key fields: BUKRS, BELNR, GJAHR,
BUZEI).
This can cause the original 10,000 REGUC key records to
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter309

=====PAGE 310=====
Column
Description
become more than 10,000 REGUP data records, e.g.
12,000.
The Total records display is then adjusted; in this case, it
increases by 2,000. The Processed records column is only
filled when writing the file and would then contain 12,000.
Why is the number of processed data records in the MODIFY and
SUMMATION modes higher than the number of data records in
the database?
For the MODIFY and SUMMATION modes, the number of data
records imported with INSERT or UPDATE is displayed in the Pro-
cessed records field. If a data record occurs multiple times in dif-
ferent packages or already exists in the database, the number of
processed data records may be higher than the number of data
records in the database.
Runtime
The Runtime column displays the total of the real runtime and the pre-
paration time. The real runtime is the total time from the start of the exe-
cution (starting after the preparation) until the completion of the
executed entity. The real runtime does not include any pauses (times
when the corresponding entity was not being processed by any pro-
cess). Because the preparation time is included, a runtime is already
displayed even if the entities are prepared but not executed. The cor-
responding tooltip shows the division of the runtime into preparation
time and execution time (real runtime).
Start time
The start time of the processing of the corresponding entity is displayed
here. For blocks, this is the start time of the first preparation. For tables, it
is the time when a process first started to process the table. For objects, it
is the start time of the first processed table. At the run level, it is the start
time of the block that started first.
End time
This display is not enabled by default, but it can be shown. It displays
when the associated entity was completed and last used by the system.
Limitations
Displays parameter restrictions for data objects in template runs. Can con-

3.5.7.10.3.1 Creating Runs
This chapter describes how to create a run.
Prerequisites
A scenario has been created.
Proceed as follows to create a run:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click Transformation.

3.5.7.10.4.6 Storing Export Files
Export files (also uploads of virtual tables) are stored in the following subfolder structure:
[share] / Scenario ID / Block PO ID / Table PO ID /
The subfolders are automatically generated and the files are stored in them, provided that the
executing user has the necessary authorizations to execute system calls.
NOTE
If customers remove the authorizations for security reasons, the files are written directly
to the share as usual.

3.5.7.10.6.1 Creating Import Blocks
Import blocks provide the framework for importing already exported data into a target system.
This chapter describes how to create an import block.
Prerequisites
For the import, data objects and tables must be available as exported data in the import dir-
ectory.
The export block containing the data objects and tables must be complete.
A target system must have been created in the system administration.
It might be necessary to delete the data in the target system before the import.
Proceed as follows to create an import block:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click
Transformation.
2. Go to the Transformation tab.
3. Right-click a run.
4. Click Create block > Import/delete.
The Create transformation block window opens.
5. Assign a name.
NOTE
The block type IMP indicates that it is an import.
6. Specify the number of processes.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter334

=====PAGE 335=====
NOTE
These are the batch processes that the Transformation Cockpit uses on the tar-
get system. This allows for the parallel processing of imports.
NOTE
Process distribution during import
Processes are distributed to different tables by default. This distribution is used
to avoid lock problems.
Tables that can only be processed by one process (tables with table locks)
have priority. The tables that are processed with the fewest processes are the
first to be assigned when processes become available.
Tables without packages are no longer the last tables to be processed but are
handled according to the above-mentioned priority. This behavior has no
impact on the import sequence that you define. If you have defined an import
sequence, the tables are processed according to the import sequence as
described in the schema above.
7. Select a block mode.
NOTE
If you select the modes Modify or Delete for the block, the settings you make
for the tables are overwritten.
Mode
Description
INSERT
Data records are inserted into the table with the SQL command INSERT
(standard).
INSERT_
ADK
Data records are inserted into the table. Duplicate keys are ignored and do
not lead to errors.
UPDATE
Data records are processed with the SQL command UPDATE. Only data
records that already exist are changed.
MODIFY
If data records are already available, they are processed with UPDATE.
Otherwise, they are processed with INSERT.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter335

=====PAGE 336=====
Mode
Description
DELETE
Data records are deleted.
8. Specify whether the rule base is used or not.
Option
Description
With rule
base
Global rules, field rules and all import events are applied during the exe-
cution.
Without rule
base
No global rules, field rules or import events are applied to the data
records from the file system.
9. Enter the source system alias of the system.
NOTE
If you do not specify an alias, the block is executed on the system that has
been defined as the default target system. In doing so, you determine which
exported data is to be imported. This applies to the entire import block.
If you assign explicit exports (right-click the block and enable the Select export
option), the source system alias is not valid for these tables/objects.
If you have specified neither a source system alias nor an export table expli-
citly, an error message is displayed during the execution.
10. Enter the target system alias of the system on which the import is to be performed.
11. Click
OK.
The block is created and displayed in the tree.

Save.

Save.

Behavior
Assignment from the source system and target system alias of the new import block if you create

Scenario with one source system and target system:

Scenario with multiple source systems and target systems:
The source system is maintained for the export block:

scenario.
No source system is maintained for the export block:

scenario.
You can select the target system from the target systems maintained in the
scenario.
Assignment from the source system and target system alias of the new import block if you create
multiple import blocks: 
Scenario with one source system and target system:
The new import blocks use the default system.
Scenario with multiple source systems and target systems:
The new import blocks are created without a system assignment.

3.5.7.10.6.6 Starting Import Blocks as Simulations (Background)
In simulation mode, the import is performed, but no data is written to the database. This allows
you to find out whether the import would lead to errors. You can repeat the simulation as often
as you want. Once an import has started, you can no longer run a simulation.
NOTE
During the execution of a simulation, two checks are performed.
1. Check:
Check for duplicate keys within the processing package
More specifically, it is checked whether the application of the rule base causes duplic-
ate keys within the processing package.
Restriction: The check takes place only if the mode of the table is not NO_IMPORT.
2. Check:
Check whether keys already exist in the database table
More specifically, it is checked whether data records that already exist in the data-
base table might be imported.
Restriction: The check takes place only if the mode of the table is not NO_IMPORT.
If a conflict is found, the keys of the table containing the erroneous data record are
saved as a warning in the log.
The system logs a maximum of 100 errors per table and process.
Proceed as follows to start the simulation:
1. Right-click an import block.
2. Click the Properties entry.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter340

=====PAGE 341=====
3. The Import block window opens.
4. Enable the Simulation option with the value X.
5. Click Simulate block.
6. Click
OK.
The simulation has started.
The simulated block can be identified by the Simulation prefix.
The status of the import changes to Running.
NOTE
The import may take some time.
7. If the block has already been simulated and has the status Erroneous or Incomplete, you
can simulate the import again via the context menu Start block in background.
3.5.7.10.6.7 Starting Import Blocks in dialog as Simulations
In simulation mode, the import is performed, but no data is written to the database. This allows
you to find out whether the import would lead to errors. You can repeat the simulation as often
as you want.
Prerequisite: 
The block has the status Unprocessed.
You can only use tables that have been exported successfully.
Once an import has started, you can no longer run a simulation.

1. Check:

Restriction: The check takes place only if the mode of the table is not NO_IMPORT.
If a conflict is found, the keys of the table containing the erroneous data record are
saved as a warning in the log.

3.5.7.10.13 Restarting Stopped/Terminated Entities
This chapter describes how to restart a run, block, an object or a table after it has been stopped
or terminated.
An entity can be stopped during processing or be terminated by the system due to errors. Stop-
ping an entity corresponds to terminating it. In both cases, it is possible to restart the entity.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter352

=====PAGE 353=====
If an entity has been stopped, you can change the processing properties such as the number of
processes. Changes to the entity itself are always transferred. Changes to table and object
sequences or to properties are only applied to objects and tables that have not been fully
executed.
If an entity has been completely processed, it cannot be restarted.
NOTE
The export method is copied to the transformation table when creating it. Changes to
tables in data objects are therefore not transferred to already created or newly started
blocks.
Prerequisites
The entity has been stopped or terminated.
Proceed as follows to restart an entity:

Transformation.
2. Go to the Transformation tab.
3. Right-click an entity.
4. Optional: Click Properties to change the properties for processing the entity.
5. Click
a. Restart <entity> in background.
1. Click Yes to confirm the operation.
2. Decide whether you want to apply possible changes to the affected data
objects.
The operation has started.
b. Restart <entity> in dialog.
1. Click Yes to confirm the operation.
2. Decide whether you want to apply possible changes to the affected data
objects.
A new mode opens.
3. Log on to the SAP® system.
4. Select the desired events.
5. Click
Execute.
The operation has started.
6. Click
Refresh to refresh the status of the object/table.
The procedure has been completed.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter353

=====PAGE 354=====
NOTE
If you click Yes in step 5.a.2. or 5.b.2, the rule base is regenerated and all changes
made to the rule base so far are applied. For performance reasons, only actually
made changes are regenerated and applied. If you click No, the previously generated
rule base remains unchanged and only changes to the properties are applied. If an
error in the rule base led to the termination, revise the respective rule and regenerate
it afterward. Otherwise, the error will occur again and cause the entity to terminate.
Changes to the properties of tables, objects and blocks are always applied regard-
less of the rule generation.

has already been processed.

b. Go to the Log tab.
1. Double-click the Process runtime or real runtime field of any row.
The Result runtime analysis window opens.
Click
Information to obtain further details on the analysis result.
NOTE
You can also call up the runtime analysis for archived log entries.

3.5.7.10.17 Status Schema for Entities
Blocks, tables and objects can have different statuses. The statuses change depending on the
processing stage.
The following statuses are available in the Transformation Cockpit:
status
Meaning
Unprocessed
The initial state after creation.
Waiting
Dependencies are not yet fulfilled, for example, if a predecessor
block has not yet been completely executed.
Released
Dependencies are fulfilled; ready for preparation.
Preparation
Programs and tables are generated; the worklist is set up and
transferred.
Preparation
erroneous
The preparation is aborted.
Pending
The preparation is complete; ready for execution.
Running
The execution is running and currently being processed.
Scout
completed
Scouting has been completed using the SR export method. The
execution is still running.
Incomplete
The execution is not running, has not been completed yet or has
been stopped.
Unknown
The status is unknown, for example, because the executing sys-
tem is not available.
Erroneous
An error occurred during execution or it has been stopped.
Complete
The execution has been fully completed without errors.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter361

=====PAGE 362=====

3.5.7.10.23 Correcting Duplicate Keys during Import
During an update, a check for duplicate keys within the package is performed. You can ignore
errors caused by duplicate keys by enabling the function so that a complete check can be per-
formed. After the check, the error is displayed as a warning in the block. If the function is not
enabled, the block ends with an error message for the duplicate key.
Prerequisites
A new import block has been created.
Import tables have been added to the import block.
Proceed as follows to ignore possible errors caused by duplicate keys during an update:
1. Enable Update. You can do this either in block mode or in table mode.
Update in block mode:
1.
Select the Update block mode when creating a new import block.
2.
Select the From block mode in the table.
Update in table mode:
1.
Select the Update table mode of an added import table.
2. Right-click an import table.
3. Click Properties.
The Import table window opens.
4. Enable the Ignore duplicate keys option.
NOTE
If duplicate keys are now found during the check, they are displayed as a warn-
ing. The process is not terminated and the last duplicate entry is accepted.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter365

5. You can check the setting in the Log tab.

3.5.7.11.3 Process Runtime vs. Real Runtime vs. Preparation Runtime
Process runtime: The process runtime is the time that all processes combined take to process
the table. It is the time that is used for performance comparisons.
Real runtime: Real runtime: The real runtime is the total time from the start of the first process to
the end of the last process. The real runtime does not include absolute pauses (times when no
process is running).
Preparation runtime: The preparation runtime is the time it takes to prepare the table.

User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter369

=====PAGE 370=====
NOTE
The runtime is calculated from the sum of runtimes that were required for the successful
processing of all files. If the run is terminated, the runtime is calculated from the sum of
all successfully processed files plus the time of the erroneously processed ones. After a
restart and successful completion, the times from errors are no longer included.
3.5.7.11.6 Displaying Processed Data and the Average Throughput per
Process
The Throughput column displays the data throughput of an ongoing transformation at the table
level in the log. The throughput is calculated as follows: amount of already processed data
divided by the time elapsed. The throughput indicates how much data is processed on average.
This provides insights as to whether long runtimes are caused by too much data being pro-
cessed, a rule base that is too slow, or complex SELECT statements. For more information,
refer to the chapter Content of the Data Scope.

3.5.7.11.15 Content of the Data Scope
3.5.7.11.15.1 Export
The data size is calculated based on the size of the internal table before the table is written to
the file system.
SR Scout Reader (Standard): With the Scout Reader procedure, the data throughput is 0. The
data throughput is only displayed when package processing is started, because no data is pro-
cessed during the Scout itself. However, the time required for the Scout is later included in the
calculation of the data throughput.
DR Direct Reader: With the Direct Reader procedure, the data throughput is calculated as soon
as data is found.
3.5.7.11.15.2 Import
The data size is calculated based on the internal table after the rule base has been applied to
the table. Because this table is processed per package, the throughput is only updated once the
first package of an import has been processed.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter373

=====PAGE 374=====
3.5.7.11.15.3 Forerunners
This function works similar to import blocks. However, for the same number of packages to be
processed, the data throughput will be higher in the case of forerunners, because no database
operations are performed.
3.5.7.11.15.4 Upload
Before the upload, the size of the internal table is determined here. The data throughput is cal-
culated based on the scheme explained previously. Because upload blocks generally have very
short runtimes, the data throughput will be significantly higher than for all other blocks.
3.5.7.11.15.5 Note
In case of two systems with different code pages in the transformation landscape, the data
size can vary considerably, although the readable variant of the table looks identical.
Even if the execution time is less than one second, it is set to one second for the cal-
culation.
The display in the Log tab is set to one process by default. This means that this figure
indicates the amount of data that a process would process in a given time.

3.5.7.13 Jumping to the Log
Double-click a row in the progress bar.
Go to the Protocol tab. The protocol is displayed.
How are the tables weighted?
The weighting is given in descending order.
1. Records of the tables (export or import records)
As soon as export and import records become available within an object, they are
determined and used for the weighting. If there are no records for a table, the table
size is used.
2. Size of the tables or table numbers
If tables within an object have a size, it is relevant for the weighting. Otherwise, the
number of all tables and the progress is calculated.
In the Progress column, the estimated progress is displayed in ~%.
What is the remaining runtime?
The remaining runtime indicates the time that is still needed until the object is completely
processed.
∞is mainly displayed for objects with a runtime of 0 and a status other than complete or
unprocessed.
The remaining runtime is determined using the current progress and the object runtime.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter376

=====PAGE 377=====
How is the object status determined?
The start timestamp of tables is used to determine the current status.
Tables from different transformation objects are taken into account as long as they refer to
the same object in the same system.
Click
Information on the progress bar to obtain more information.

REFRESH_EXEC: Updates the status information of an ongoing exe-
cution.
SEND_EMAILS: Sends status e-mails.
START_PENDING_EXEC: Starts an execution once the preparation has
been completed. This action also starts the processes in the satellite sys-
tem.
START_WAITING_EXEC: Checks if an execution waiting for depend-
encies can be started and starts the execution, if necessary.
STOP_EXECUTION: Stops executions.
TAB_STAT_REFRESH: Starts the (DB) table statistics and updates the
status for table statistics.

3.6.4 Analyzing Database Indexes
You can analyze database indexes. The analysis compares all fields used for the selection of a
table with the indexes in the table and the primary keys of the table. Thus it is checked how
many of the fields used for the selection are covered by an index. The information is determined
in the system at runtime.
Proceed as follows to carry out the analysis:
1. In the left-hand navigation bar, click
Data objects.
2. In the menu bar, click Functions > Analyze DB indexes.
The program Analysis of DB indexes for fields from selections of tables opens.
3. Specify a scenario.
4. Optional: Make further restrictions by specifying the module, object and table.
5. Click
Execute.
The analysis is carried out.
The result is displayed in a table.
Double-clicking a row directs you to the corresponding table of the scenario.
Status information
The status indicates how effectively the index covers the selection fields.
Green: The index covers more than 90% of the table selection.
Yellow: The index covers more than 60% of the table selection.
Red: The index covers less than 60% of the table selection.
Red X: The selection is not covered by an index.
Filter options
The toolbar allows you to filter the displayed result. The function of the button changes accord-
ing to the selected option:
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter392

=====PAGE 393=====
All: Displays all indexes
Only highest coverage: Displays only the indexes of the table that reach the highest
coverage.
3.6.5 Importing CSV Files
You have the option to import files that were exported from non-SAP ® systems and saved in
CSV format into the Transformation Cockpit. You can then write these files into the tables of the
SAP® target system during the import. 
Consider the following when importing the files:
Each file must have a header line designating the columns in the table. 
The files can have an independent structure.
Fields that do not correspond to the target structure are not considered during the import.
The data structure is not checked.
The export rule base is not taken into account. 
The assignment of CSV files is only possible at the table level.

Preparatory Work

Back up your scenario to avoid data loss. For further information, refer to the Downloading Scen-
ario chapter.

report in the central system.

float16/decfloat34
The export/import as well as the syntax check of a table with a field that uses one of
the two data types are possible without problems.

3.6.12 Moving Scenarios to Another Control System
You can move scenarios from one control system to another. This function is useful if the current
control system can no longer be used. This is the case, for example, if the source and target sys-
tems are used simultaneously as the control system and the SAP system itself needs to be
updated after a transformation test run.
Two data centers that are not connected is another use case for moving a control system. Also
in this case, the source system is simultaneously used as the control system. Transformation
exports are performed exclusively in the source data center. Prior to Release 22.09, /SNP/*
tables had to be subsequently downloaded and imported into the corresponding control system
of the target data center.
Release 22.11 now ensures a convenient scenario download and upload instead of transferring
all /SNP/* tables. This is enabled by the following additional options for the functions scenario
download and scenario upload:
The transformation status of all involved tables, blocks and runs can be downloaded from
and uploaded to the same or to a new control system – together with all the information
required for the transformation.
Optionally, you can include logged messages.
Backups (and their restores) retain their status values.
NOTE
The transformation status values and messages consume a lot of memory. After the exe-
cution, many messages appear, and the transformation status contains metadata for
each written export file. This additional data can cause memory issues during scenario
downloads and uploads.
NOTE
These files are usually stored in a generated subfolder with the ID of the scenario. If the
source file path is /src and the scenario ID is SCEN_ABC, all folders/export files will be
written to /src/SCEN_AB. If the file path of the target system is /tgt and the new scenario
ID is SCEN_XYZ, the files from /src/SCEN_AB must be available in /tgt/SCEN_XYZ. In
addition, the operating system user in the target system must be able to read the files
and directories.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter399

=====PAGE 400=====
3.6.13 Generating Offsets
You have the option to generate offsets by using a report. The report analyzes the specified
tables and fields (domains) and sets up the segmentations in an offset. The fields are con-
sidered in the original sequence of the table during the generation. Filtered fields are completely
ignored and do not move the segments.
EXAMPLE
Table A006
MANDT MANDT CLNT 3
KAPPL KAPPL CHAR 2
KSCHL KSCHA CHAR 4
VKORG VKORG CHAR 4
VTWEG VTWEG CHAR 2
PLTYP PLTYP CHAR 2
WAERK WAERK CUKY 5
MATNR MATNR CHAR 18
DATBI KODATBI DATS 8
DATAB KODATAB DATS 8
KNUMH KNUMH CHAR 10
If you generate the segmentation for the above mentioned table, the result is:
MANDT(0,3), KAPPL(3,2), KSCHL(5,4), VKORG(9,4), VTWEG(13,2) ...
If you exclude the MANDT and KSCHL fields instead, the result is:
KAPPL(0,2), VKORG(2,4), VTWEG(6,2) ...
The segmentations always start with 0 and are generated without any gaps.
If you have selected the Conditions parameter set, a corresponding condition is set
to identify the table for each segmentation.
Use case (primary):
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter400

=====PAGE 401=====
Generating the offset for condition tables
Customers can create condition tables (A*/B*/KOT*/...) according to their require-
ments; therefore, they differ from customer to customer. However, there are spe-
cifications for the structure because the data is also stored in other tables (e.g. in
KONH in a non-transparent field). So that the entries can be assigned between
KONH and the customer tables, an offset with the corresponding segmentations
must be created.
NOTE
To generate the offset for condition tables, you can use the CONDITIONS variant that is
also contained in the delivery.
The following section describes how to generate an offset.
Prerequisites
An offset with scope has been created.

1. Click
Global in the left-hand navigation bar.

The program Transformation Cockpit – Offset Generator opens.

4. Select an offset for which you want to create segmentations and parameters.
5. Adjust the following settings according to your requirements:
Settings area
Clean up segment. and param.: The option is enabled by default. If seg-
mentations/parameters are already maintained in the offset, they are deleted if the
option is enabled.
Create parameter set area
Parameters for conditions: Adds parameters to the offset and generates the con-
ditions of the offsets according to the parameters. This is a special type of offset for
specific use cases. Currently, parameter sets can only be generated for conditions.
No parameters: No parameters are added.
Selection of tables and fields area
Tables/fields: Specify the tables/fields for which the segmentations are to be gen-
erated.
Consider only key fields: Restricts the generation to key fields of the table
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter401

=====PAGE 402=====
6. Click
Execute.
The offset has been generated.

3.6.34 Remote SE16 (Displaying Table Contents)
Transaction SE16 is used to display table contents. Therefore, you no longer need to jump to the
source system/target system to view the table contents. Using this transaction, you can access
the table contents from the control system.
Proceed as follows to remotely view table contents:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/CN_SE16.
The Remote SE16 view opens.
2. Enter the RFC connection of the system whose table contents you want to view.
3. Enter the table whose content you want to view.
4. Click
Execute.
The Contents of <table name> on <system name> view opens. In general, the interface
provides the key fields of the table in order to select data.
5. Enter a value that you want to search for, or leave the fields empty and execute one of the
available functions.
The following functions are available:
Display data: The data of the table is displayed with the selection criteria you spe-
cified.
Export to .xlsx: The selected data is exported to Excel. Enter a target directory
and a file name.
Count records: The number of data records according to your selection criteria is
displayed.
Change fields: A window opens where you can add additional fields to the table
in order to further restrict the selection criteria for data records.
Technical field names: You can use the button to switch between technical and
descriptive field names. The technical field names of the table are displayed instead
of their description texts. The button text changes to Descriptive field names.
Data quality: The data quality of the data records is checked against the selected
table on another system according to your selection criteria. First, a window for
entering the RFC connection to the system against which the data quality is to be
checked opens. After confirming the RFC connection, the check is executed and the
result displayed. You will receive information on the fields’ fill level in % and the num-
ber of filled fields. The system also displays the percentage of valid field values and
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter418

=====PAGE 419=====
the number of valid fields. The number of unique values and the maximum length of

Refresh: The view is refreshed if changes are made in another session at the

Technical field names: see above
Export to .xlsx.: see above
Data quality: see above
Influencing factors: Influencing factors for a column are determined. The influ-
encing factors are displayed in a new window with the probability of their occur-
rence.
3.6.35 File Encryption
To protect personal data, it is necessary to encrypt personal data. The Transformation Cockpit
allows you to encrypt the data after it has been compressed and before it is exported. During the
import, you can decrypt the data again before decompressing.
Various tables from the HR environment are encrypted by default; this corresponds to the scen-
ario * in the table /SNP/TE00TABENCR.
The encryption applies to all exports that are started after setting the password as well as to the
scenario itself. The password must be maintained in the scenario configuration before the
export. The encryption status is stored per written export file. Therefore, when displaying the
export files or during the import, the correct password for the encrypted files must be stored in
the scenario.
If the files are encrypted with another password because you changed the password during the
migration, the files cannot be displayed or imported. The same applies if you delete the pass-
word during the migration (empty password).
NOTE
Performance
Encryption extends the runtime of tables by approx. 30% if the system provides suf-
ficient CPU power. The runtime can multiply on slower systems.
Prerequisites
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter419

=====PAGE 420=====
A scenario has been created.
Proceed as follows to encrypt data: 
1. Start transaction SE16.
Das Programm Data Browser: Initial Screen opens.
2. In the Table Name field, enter the table /SNP/TE00TABENCR.
3. Click
Create Entries.
NOTE
The tables to be encrypted are maintained in this table.
The program Table /SNP/TE00TABENCR Insert opens.
4. In the Scenario ID field, enter the ID of the scenario in which you want to encrypt data.
5. In the Pattern field, enter a pattern for the encryption.
NOTE
The wildcard * encrypts HR data by default. If you enter MA*, for example, all
tables that start with MA are encrypted.
6. Click
Save.
7. Go to your scenario.
8. In the left-hand navigation bar, click Data objects.
9. Double-click the scenario in the data object tree.
The detail area for the scenario is displayed.
10. Go to the Run parameters tab.
11. Specify an Encryption password.
12. Click
Save.
You have prepared the encryption.
All exports that you perform are encrypted according to your specifications. The scenario
is also encrypted.

3.6.39 Deleting Data from /SNP/TE* Tables
WARNING
Deleting data can affect the execution in other scenarios. This is because custom tables
can be used in the rule base of scenarios, which cannot be evaluated. Therefore, only
delete the data if you no longer need it in other scenarios.
WARNING
Generated tables can no longer be deleted by the report if they are not connected to a
scenario. The connection to a scenario is removed if the runtime information is deleted
without also deleting the generated tables. Therefore, only delete the runtime inform-
ation if you also delete the generated tables at the same time.
Proceed as follows to delete data from /SNP/TE* tables or simulate the deletion:
1. Start transaction SE38.
2. In the Program field, enter the report /SNP/TE05_CLEANUP.
3. Click
Execute.
The view Clean up /SNP/TE* tables opens.
4. Select one or more scenarios that you want to clean up. Alternatively, enable the Delete
all data option.
5. Specify whether you want to perform a simulation.
NOTE
If you execute a simulation, the system shows which tables and values would be deleted
from the tables. The deletion is performed if you execute report again without using this
option.
6. Select whether you want to delete the values from all tables or only from specific tables
(/SNP/TE05DKP and/or /SNP/TE05ESEL and /SNP/TE05ESELC).
7. Select whether you want to delete Database selection tables.
8. Select whether you want to delete Database mapping tables.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter425

=====PAGE 426=====
9. Select whether you only want to delete the Values or also the Database tables in case of
own tables.
NOTE
Because own tables can be defined across scenarios, data is only deleted if it is clearly
assigned to a scenario.
10. Optional: Delete the collected domain usage values from the tables /SNP/TE0XDOMU
and /SNP/TE0XDOMUCNT.
11. Click
Execute.
You have deleted the data from the tables.

4 SNP S/4HANA Cockpit
4.1 About the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit
You can use the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit to convert data from the classic SAP® ECC data model
to the new, simplified SAP® S/4HANA data model. It is a tool for migrating data to the
SAP® S/4HANA data model in the Financial Accounting and Logistics areas.
In addition to these two areas, utility programs are included to help you with the imple-
mentation. The SNP S/4HANA Cockpit is operated in the SAP® GUI.
The application is based on standard SAP tools that have been used so far in brownfield con-
versions of the system. The SNP S/4HANA Cockpit extends these functions to support new use
cases and provide you with comprehensive help.
The SNP S/4HANA Cockpit is designed for different use cases. The two most important use
cases are described below.
4.1.1 Migration to an Empty Target System
This case requires the target of the migration to be an empty or non-production system. All data
in the original tables of the ECC data model is completely converted into the target structures.
4.1.2 Migration into a Production System
This case requires the existence of productively used application data in the target structures of
the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit system. By processing selected data records, it is possible to convert
only newly added company codes. All existing data is left in its current state. The following
restrictions apply in order to correctly delineate the data records:
No merging into existing company codes
The following chapters describe how to operate the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit.
4.2 Adjusting the Registry Table
To adjust the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit, a registry table is available. You can use table entries to
change default values, enable additional functions or change certain behavior.

tional transports into the system, you might need to perform this step again at a later time.

CDS views are generated before the class is generated. If you select both options,
the generation is automatically performed in the correct order.

6. Optional: Enable the New G/L active option.
7. Click
Execute.
The generation has been started.

shows whether the CDS views were generated successfully. Additional information, warn-
ings and error messages are displayed here, if available.

4.4.2.8 NZD Delta Load
In the NZD delta load area, you can perform delta-related operations. The area is divided into
further areas:
4.4.2.8.1 NZD Preparation
In the NZD preparation subdirectory, you can call the following two functions:
4.4.2.8.1.1 Creating Log Tables
WARNING
This area is only available in systems as of release SAP® S/4HANA 19.09.
This chapter describes how to create, delete or display log tables for NZD preparation. These
tables are a prerequisite for a successful NZD conversion. Log tables are created in the Z*
namespace.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter454

=====PAGE 455=====
NOTE
For the NZD delta migration in the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit, log tables exist to enable
the delta migration.
To fill the log tables, you can use an API that can be called within the rule base of the
Transformation Cockpit. First, the log tables are filled and then transferred to the trig-
ger tables using the function Fill FINS_MIG* tables. Use the following API for log
tables:
/snp/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>get_instance( iv_module = /sn-
p/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>co_finance iv_original_tabname = <tab-
name of original table> )->insert_delta( it_data = <lt_data> iv_
operation = 'I' ).
The API is executed with Modify by default. You can use the iv_mode parameter to
control whether the API is inserted via insert_adk.
You can use the optional parameter iv_description to add a description in order to
determine the original location of a record for a run.
NOTE
Data of a table is always stored with a specific name. You can use the method GET_
LOGGING_TABLE to receive the corresponding name of this table again.
/snp/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>get_instance( iv_module = /sn-
p/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>co_finance iv_original_tabname = <tab-
name of original table> )->get_logging_table( ).
Proceed as follows to create log tables:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/S4.
The SNP S/4HANA Cockpit program opens.
2. In the left-hand navigation bar, click
Financial Accounting >
NZD delta load > 
NZD preparation >
Create log tables.
3. In the Prefix field, enter the value ZSNP.
4. In the Execution type field, select the appropriate name depending on the desired action.

4.4.2.10.1 Stopping and Restarting Runs and Steps
Proceed as follows to stop runs or steps in the run monitor:
1. Right-click a run or step.
2. Enable the option Stop run (for an active run) or Stop step (for an active step).
The run or step has been stopped.
Proceed as follows to restart runs or steps in the run monitor:
1. Right-click a stopped run or step.
2. Enable the option Restart run (for a stopped run) or Restart step (for a stopped step).
The run or step has been restarted.
4.4.2.10.2 Restarting Failed Runs
You can restart failed runs with the run type ACTIVE. You can also use the function if there are
additional failed packages.
Proceed as follows to restart failed runs:
1. In the structure tree, click the failed run.
2. Right-click the run.
3. Select the Restart run function.
A query opens, asking if you want to start the run.
4. Confirm the query with Yes.
5. The Run parameters window opens.
6. Optional: Specify whether you want to perform the Execution in the background.
7. Specify the number of background processes.
8. Optional: Specify whether to include Erroneous steps.
9. Specify the Server group or change the existing server group.
The erroneous run has been restarted.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter470

=====PAGE 471=====
NOTE
Archived runs cannot be restarted. Runs with the processing status Completed or
Running cannot be restarted either. However, if a run is completed from a process
perspective, it can contain functional errors. To avoid duplicate keys, it is not pos-
sible to restart these runs either. For archived runs, only the Display run option is
available.

/snp/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>get_instance( iv_module = /sn-
p/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>co_logistic iv_original_tabname = <tab-
name of original table> )->insert_delta( it_data = <lt_data> iv_
operation = 'I' ).
The API is executed with Modify by default. You can use the iv_mode parameter to
control whether the API is inserted via insert_adk.

LOGGING_TABLE to receive the corresponding name of this table again.
/snp/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>get_instance( iv_module = /sn-
p/px4x_cl_nzd_tab_factory=>co_logistic iv_original_tabname = <tab-
name of original table> )->get_logging_table( ).

4.4.4.8.3 Reasons for Line Item Exits
During line item migrations, the documents to be converted are identified by their AWKEY. Dur-
ing this process, selected organizational units are searched. Based on this search, the system
determines which documents are converted.
Problems can occur in the following cases:
1. In case of internal transactions
2. No organizational units exist in the AWKEY
3. Conversion at different times
NOTE
It is possible that data must be migrated and converted several times. Already exist-
ing data must not be changed.
4. Migration into an already filled company code
NOTE
It is possible that data must be migrated and converted several times. Already exist-
ing data must not be changed.

4.5.1 Copying Customizing Between Clients
The SNP S/4HANA Cockpit uses client-dependent customizing. In some cases, this customizing
may not be available in the client in which you want to perform the conversion. In this case, you
can use the report /SNP/S4_TRANSFER_CUSTOMIZING. You can use the report to copy the
required customizing settings from a corresponding client. You can specify a source client and a
target client in the report.
4.5.2 Custom Exit for Controlling the Line Item Migration
This chapter describes how to control the line item migration using a custom exit.
4.5.2.1 Motivation
In line item migration, the documents to be converted are identified by their AWKEY. The
routines search in the field for the selected organizational units. This decides which documents
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter503

=====PAGE 504=====
will be converted.
Problems can occur in several cases:
Intercompany business
The AWKEY contains a different organizational unit than the one to be migrated. This is
the case, for example, if the document chain began in a different company code. The
method described here must therefore be used.
No organizational units in AWKEY
The reference key (AWKEY) for documents of certain reference procedures (AWTYP) is
not made up of relevant organizational units for packaging. To obtain information on the
composition of the reference keys for each reference procedure, you can consult the table
/SNP/S4_AWKEYOFF in the SAP system (e.g. using transaction SE16). In this case, the
framework ensures that all documents for this reference procedure are processed at the
single record level.
Conversion at different times
It is possible that data must be migrated and converted multiple times. Therefore, it is
important to perform this step cautiously in order to avoid modifying already existing data
on the system.
Migration to an already filled company code
It is possible that data must be migrated and converted multiple times. Therefore, it is
important to perform this step cautiously in order to avoid modifying already existing data
on the system.
4.5.2.2 Function
This method addresses an additional exit (function module) during line item migration. All doc-
ument headers (BKPF, COBK) or assets (ANEP, ANLP) of a single AWTYP are delivered to this
module simultaneously. You can use individual ABAP® code to exclude documents or assets
from this set as required. All documents or assets that the module returns are then further pro-
cessed.

6 Staging
NOTE

NOTE

actions:
Online video for the transaction
Online help for the latest version

6.1 Introduction to Staging
A staging area, or landing zone, is an intermediate storage area used for data processing during
the extract, transform and load process (ETL). The data staging area is located between the
data source(s) and the data target(s). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staging_(data)).
The following chapters describe how the staging function can be used to minimize the downtime
in conversion projects.
6.1.1 Staging Manager Types
The staging manager type determines the staging method used, i.e. the technical imple-
mentation of the staging.
The DDIC staging manager generally uses shadow tables that are available in the DDIC. As a
result, the data switch can take place in significantly less time. This is relevant for minimizing the
downtime.
The client staging manager uses different clients in a naming structure from AAA–ZZZ. No data
structures need to be generated or changed for this purpose.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter512

=====PAGE 513=====
NOTE
We still expect to add additional staging manager types, e.g. to use file systems.
6.1.2 Methodology for Using the Staging Framework
In the context of SNP transformations, a staging area can be used to store data before importing
it into a target system or to perform conversions and deletions within the same system.
6.1.2.1 Implemented Business Cases
Downtime minimization in conversions (in combination with (RB)NZD function)
Downtime minimization (with (RB)NZD) – or at least very quick selective deletion of data –
with the added benefit of a paper bin function from which data can be restored
Foreign Key Check after applying all mappings and import rules, but without actually writ-
ing data to the target. This enables independent tests of individual objects or com-
prehensive test imports, without having to reset the relevant target system afterwards.
Isolated individual tests within a system (import into the same system) and comparisons of
different test systems (e.g. by transferring and validating customizing from the target sys-
tem to the source system)
Recording of all data changes in the context of a conversion or migration (complete trans-
formation log) and, based on this, the possibility of undoing all changes made or parts of it
6.1.3 Minimizing Downtime During Conversions
6.1.3.1 Visualization
This section explains the following visualization step by step from left to right.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter513

=====PAGE 514=====
6.1.3.1.1 Activating Delta Logging for the Tables in Scope
The NZD procedure requires delta logging to be activated so that changes from this point in time
onward can be migrated in delta migrations. There are currently two ways to implement NZD in
the SNP software portfolio. One is part of the software component Client Migration and the other
is RBNZD, which is best combined with the Transformation Cockpit. Activating delta logging for
tables in scope will generate shadow tables (also known as “trigger tables”) and database trig-
gers on the system.
6.1.3.1.2 Initial Sequential Data Migration
Initially, the complete content of the tables with conversion rules is imported into the staging
area. The complete data can be imported into staging via a TC scenario or staging can be gen-
erated with the complete data contents of the original tables. For migrations using the Trans-
formation Cockpit, transformation rules can be applied to the complete set of data or parts of it.
At this stage, it is also possible to generate or reduce data. There are no restrictions for the way
transformations are defined, except that every write access must be piped into the staging frame-
work (into the DB Access Interceptor Class). Any selections that are defined lead to the
excluded data being deleted in a later step.
6.1.3.1.3 RBNZD Delta Loads
Once the initial data migration and conversion have been completed, collector jobs combine
changes to the data into selection tables. These tables correspond to the root tables in the TC
scenario. As a result, every table that is placed directly within a transformation object and read
directly – not only through table relations – receives a corresponding selection table as a form of
preselection table. This means that a table is selected depending on its selection table, so that
only the data objects for which changes have been logged are deleted in the target and re-trans-
ferred.
As a result of repeated delta loads, data in the staging area is kept up to date. The only dif-
ference is that during the delta load, the same conversion rules that were used in the initial
sequential migration are applied to data in the delta loads as well. Continuous collector loads
and delta loads are used to maintain this situation until a maintenance window is reached; the
cutover is then performed in this maintenance window. The RBNZD procedure and these delta
loads thus allow that the system can be used productively during the data conversion, and the
subsequent maintenance window becomes smaller.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter514

=====PAGE 515=====
Once the data conversion is complete and you are waiting for the maintenance window, you can
already use Data Consistency Verification to verify that customizing data and master data exist
for the data in the staging area. This makes it possible to detect and correct any errors and
incompleteness shortly before the cutover.
6.1.3.1.4 Final Delta Load
As soon as the appointed time for the maintenance window is reached, the system is locked
down. During migrations, all productive users are locked, all batch processes halted and all inter-
faces blocked. A final delta load is performed to transfer the last changes from the original data-
base tables into the staging area. Downtime migration activities can also begin. These activities
typically affect a large number of tables that contain relatively small amounts of data. After the
final delta load, delta logging is disabled so that it does not interfere with the next step.
NOTE
Until this point, no changes have been made to the original database tables. If Data Con-
sistency Verification identifies any major inconsistencies, you can simply disable delta
logging and delete shadow tables (fallback scenario).
6.1.3.1.5 Switching Data with Staging
To carry out the conversion with minimal downtime, the staging framework is now used to switch
the data between the staging area and the original client. The best staging manager mode for
this is mode D. This mode uses DDIC shadow tables to store data. The switch then takes place
by simply renaming the database tables. This results in a short, constant runtime, regardless of
the amount of data. Staging manager mode C, which uses UPDATE statements on the client
field for the data switch, is also much faster than a conventional conversion. However, the
runtime increases with the data amount in a linear fashion.
At this point, you must either use the staging manager type C for pool tables and cluster tables,
or accept that these tables will automatically be converted to transparent tables by switching
data with the staging area. Although this has a positive effect on system performance and
reduces the runtime of a later release upgrade of the system, it also significantly increases the
database storage requirements of the system.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter515

=====PAGE 516=====
6.1.3.1.6 Cutover Verification
Typically, once all technical steps have been completed, selective sets of cutover verification
tests are performed, including the creation of reconciliation lists such as balance sheets. The
Data Consistency Verification results can support this verification. Since Data Consistency Veri-
fication can run prior to the maintenance window, it does not affect the runtime. The old/un-
converted data can still be accessed in the staging area. Individual data records can be migrated
back into the productive tables as required during the cutover or during a hypercare phase after
the cutover.
NOTE
If the technical verification fails during the cutover and leads to a so-called “No-go
decision”, the original tables can be restored with a data switch in order to quickly undo
all conversion changes.
6.1.3.1.7 System Release and Hypercare
Once the verification has resulted in a “Go” decision, the system is unlocked. If any post-go-live
issues arise, a complete log is available from both the staging area, which still contains the data
from the original client, and from RBNZD, which has extensive logging information.
6.1.3.1.8 Deleting Logs
Since the logs contain a large volume of data – even larger than the actually converted data –
they are deleted from the system after an agreed period by an administrative intervention. The
deletion is generally very quick, since entire tables or clients are deleted.
6.1.4 Minimizing Downtime During Deletions
Using staging for selective quick deletion with a paper bin function.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter516

=====PAGE 517=====
Even without combining it with RBNZD, the staging framework can be used to mass delete data
from an SAP system very quickly. The staging framework also has the added benefit of a pos-
sible paper bin function.
6.1.4.1 Selection of Data that Is Not to Be Deleted
In the first step, a migration engine (preferably Transformation Cockpit) is used to migrate the
data that is not to be deleted into the staging area. The staging manager type D is used for trans-
parent tables; the staging manager type C is used for pool tables and cluster tables. If the dele-
tion happens as a result of a previous carve-out project, most of the selections used in the
migration scenario can be used for the deletion scenario. However, the data selection must be
cross-client, and the migration must also migrate data across all clients into the staging area. If
the amount of data to be deleted is considerably smaller than the amount of data to be pre-
served, staging with content can also be created and then deleted in staging. It may also be pos-
sible to make individual decisions for the largest tables in the system as to whether the data that
is not to be deleted should be migrated into staging or, conversely, whether all data should
(quickly) be duplicated as staging with content and then individual data deleted again.
6.1.4.2 Carrying out a Data Switch
The staging function data exchange is used during the deletion process. Technically, shadow
tables and original tables are renamed when using the staging manager type D so that they
switch places in the system. Since this is only renaming and not a data migration, the runtime of
the data switch is constant and very short. When using the staging manager type C, the client
field is updated. Original data is still available from the staging area. It can be restored if it was
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter517

=====PAGE 518=====
deleted accidentally. Individual data can even be restored during a Hypercare phase, which can
last a few days or even weeks. The staging area with the deleted data is only dropped once the
decision has been made, which immediately reduces the size of the database. This final deletion
step involves deleting entire database tables and therefore takes place in a matter of minutes,
regardless of the amount of data. It can also be performed during system uptime, since data in
the staging area is not used for productive operation of the system in any way. This last step is to
empty the paper bin, which similar to emptying the recycle bin in Windows.
The second alternative is to perform the deletion on a table-by-table basis. This means that indi-
vidual shadow tables and original tables are immediately switched after the data migration has
finished. The switched original tables are immediately dropped afterward. This quickly reduces
the database size, but it is not possible to restore data using the staging framework. A backup
before the deletion is therefore a required fallback scenario and a downtime of the system during
the deletion process recommended.
6.1.4.3 Runtime
The deletion procedure described here contrasts with the usual deletion using DELETE state-
ments. Typically, the data to be deleted must be preselected using SELECT statements and
then deleted record by record (FROM TABLE) using the primary keys. However, the separate
storage of data that cannot be deleted and the subsequent deletion of entire tables is 20 times
faster in terms of size.
The runtime of this process is mainly determined by the insertion of data into the staging area.
Since this is a plain INSERT ... FROM TABLE (with no duplicate keys), it is the fastest deletion
method SNP has implemented in a standard software product so far.
6.1.4.4 Combining Staging Deletion with RBNZD
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter518

=====PAGE 519=====
Using the staging framework for deletions, combined with RBNZD, is simpler than using the sta-
ging framework for RBNZD downtime-minimized conversions, which are described in the
chapter on Minimizing Downtime During Conversions. This chapter also contains information on
the usual steps such as locking and unlocking the system, and RBNZD aspects such as activ-
ating and deactivating logging and delta loads.
6.1.5 Using the Foreign Key Check for Staging Areas
The following visualization shows how to use the Foreign Key Check to verify data from a sta-
ging area against the check tables of a target system.
NOTE

framework.
The Data Consistency Verification supports all conceivable verification directions when val-
idating data in staging.
The following data can be verified:
Original data from production tables
Use case: You want to check data against customizing and master data that was imported
from another system into staging of the respective system. This enables a consistency
check without having to write data to a target system. In addition, the amount of master
data and customizing is smaller than the amount of transaction data, which allows checks
with reduced system sizes and runtimes.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter519

=====PAGE 520=====
Data in staging
Use case: You imported transaction data in staging into a target system and want to val-
idate it there.
New data records in staging
Use case: For consecutive DCV checks, you can use the staging framework in order to
check newly inserted data records only. This reduces the downtime by limiting the checks
to the most recent changes, rather than including all data records. For more information,
refer to the section INSERT log data checked.
The following comparison methods can be used:
Check against the original check tables of the system
Use case: Only application data is migrated; Customizing data and master data are not
part of the migration.
Check against data from staging areas of the check tables
Use case: You can verify customizing data and master data by migrating them to another
system instead of migrating the larger amount of application data. You therefore use this
option primarily when checking the original table data against staging data.
Check against a combination of original check tables and staging data for check tables
Use case: Customizing and master data are part of the migration, but data already exists
in the target system. The check should consider the data in combination as it would be
generated after importing it into the target client instead of into staging. This option should
usually be selected for checks against staging.
6.1.6 Using Staging as a Migration Log and Rolling back Data
Changes
This chapter describes in detail how to use staging to create a migration log. The migration log is
a complete record of all changes made to the database tables via the migration engine. You can
use it to answer and validate detailed questions in test cycles, but also in post-go-live support
during the hypercare phase.
The staging framework also offers the capability to roll back all changes written by the migration
engine through the logged write modes. It is even possible to supply a different target area ID
when writing and therefore differentiate changes made to tables in multiple logs and roll back
only a specific set of changes.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter520

=====PAGE 521=====
The technical principle behind the migration log is that changes which are written by the migra-
tion engine via the logged write modes of the staging framework are put into separate staging
areas. They can be retrieved from these areas, analyzed or used for a rollback.
NOTE
In order to use staging as a migration log, you must follow the guide for integrating
staging into your TC scenario. Just as you can use the standard write modes for writ-
ing to staging areas (INSERT, DELETE, MODIFY, UPDATE, INSADK), you can also
use the logged staging modes (INSLOG, DELLOG, MODLOG, LOGADK). The first
group of mentioned write modes writes data to the staging area, which is one table or
target client. The second group of write modes writes to both the actual target tables
and additionally into multiple staging clients or staging tables.
6.1.6.1 Write Mode INSLOG
Entries that are inserted into the target table are also written to a unique staging area. Both sta-
ging manager types support the logging function. Therefore, the log can be written to a shadow
table that is accessible like any other SAP database table or it can be written to a differing client,
so that no additional tables need to be generated on the system. Furthermore, as mentioned pre-
viously, a unique target area ID can be supplied, so that multiple staging clients or shadow
tables might be used in order to categorize the changes made – by object in the Transformation
Cockpit for example.
6.1.6.2 Write Mode LOGADK
For entries that are made using Insert Accepting Duplicate Keys, the data that is not written
because it is a duplicate is written to its own unique staging area. This allows a user to see
which data has not been written during an import, because this data might be erroneous. It is
also important to note that a data record which is already in the log for inserted data records will
not be written to the log for duplicates. This means that the engine itself does not create logged
duplicates if a data record is written multiple times. This would clog up the log for duplicate data
records with data records that were actually written to the target during the time the logging-write
modes were used. The only data records stored in the duplicates log are those that could not be
written to the system because of previously existing data records.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter521

=====PAGE 522=====
6.1.6.3 Write Mode DELLOG
If a data record is written using the write mode DELLOG, the entry is deleted from the target
table, but a copy of it is stored in a staging log of deleted data records unless it already exists
there (in an earlier version).
6.1.6.4 Write Mode MODLOG
The SAP-specific function MODIFY generally consists of an UPDATE (first) and then an
INSERT if the UPDATE fails. The write mode MODLOG handles this by first checking if there
are preexisting data records and then by adding them to the log for deleted data records. All data
records of the data block that are supplied to the write mode MODLOG are added to the log for
inserted data records. But if a data record is modified multiple times, only the first version of the
data record is added to the staging log for deletions, and only the last version of the data record
is added to the staging log for inserts.
6.1.6.5 Evaluating the Migration Log
In order to evaluate the content of the migration log, you can retrieve the locations of logged
data through the API by using the transaction /SNP/SG_LOCATION or /SNP/SG_LOG.
6.1.6.6 Rollback
The migration log can roll back changes. If the log is created in only one target area and no other
write mode is applied to the tables – maybe due to a system lockdown – then the rollback recre-
ates the status of a table at the point when writing to the table through the logged write modes
began.
The rollback can be executed using the transaction /SNP/SG or /SNP/SG_TC as a staging oper-
ation. You can monitor the process using the transaction /SNP/SG_MONITOR.
If multiple target areas (or staging manager types) have been used, you can roll back these
parts of the log can individually. However, be aware that the sequence of such partial rollback
operations might lead to unexpected results in such a scenario.
Changes made to the table in ways other than through the logged write modes of the staging
framework are not logged and cannot be rolled back.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter522

=====PAGE 523=====

6.1.8 Staging for Pool Tables and Cluster Tables
There are some limitations when using the staging framework for pool tables and cluster tables
because these tables are only emulated by the OpenSQL layer and are non-transparent at the
database level. Some of these limitations relate to performance, while others require the
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter523

=====PAGE 524=====
corresponding functions to be executed on the table cluster or table pool instead of the cluster
table and pool table. It might be necessary to include additional tables in the migration scope.
NOTE
If you use the direct control UI (transaction /N/SNP/SG), you are informed about
these special cases. When programming using the API, the classes will return excep-
tions in some cases.
The restrictions differ depending on the Staging Manager type, since the Staging Manager types
are implemented to use different methods:
Note that, with regard to the effects on the migration strategy, the data switch is generally much
faster with the DDIC Shadow Table Staging Manager than with the Client Staging Manager. The
main advantage of the Client Staging Manager is that it does not require shadow tables and
does not convert pool tables and cluster tables into transparent tables during the switch. You
could use the DDIC Staging Manager for transparent tables if a quick switch is required, and the
Client Staging Manager for pool tables and cluster tables if you do not yet want to convert them
to transparent tables. However, with the introduction of SAP HANA® at the latest, relevant tables
must become transparent. The runtime of an upgrade can be shortened by making these tables
transparent beforehand.
NOTE
When using the staging manager type D, you are not allowed to create shadow
tables for pool tables that have more than 16 primary key fields. The reason is that
shadow tables are created as transparent tables and the SAP system does not allow
more than 16 primary key fields.

you receive an error message and the operation is terminated.

6.2 Integrating Staging into Existing TC Scenarios
You can easily integrate staging functions into any Transformation Cockpit scenario. Combining
staging with RBNZD can reduce the downtime of conversion projects and deletions. Executing
the Foreign Key Check on shadow tables shortens the check runtime and reduces the need for a
comparison run.

6.2.2 Global ZAPI Functions
6.2.2.1 Creating Global ZAPI Functions
To pipe data into the staging area instead of the actual target tables, you need to direct it toward
the class /SNP/SG05_CL_DB_ACC_INTERCE (DB Access Interceptor). This is an API/facade
class with class documentation in the system. The data is piped through global functions that are
scheduled to become API calls in the near future.
There is one global function for each of the TC import modes, and one generic global function
that takes import modes into account from the environment variables. The TC behavior should
be the same, except that data is written to the staging area if ZAPI functions are being used. To
integrate staging into your scenario, first create the global functions as listed below.

import mode into account

WHEN 'INSERT'.
PERFORM zapi_insert USING ct_data.
WHEN 'UPDATE'.
PERFORM zapi_update USING ct_data.
WHEN 'MODIFY'.
PERFORM zapi_modify USING ct_data.
WHEN 'INSERT_ADK'.

6.2.5 Fast Deletion via Data Switch
To delete large amounts of data quickly, it is possible to transfer all data that you do not want to
delete into a shadow table and then conduct a data switch. The original data will be still available
in the shadow table and can be used as a backup.

tables in the deletion operation, which executes the global function ZAPI_INSERT. You then
need to decide whether you want to automatically switch the data in the shadow table and ori-

You can switch data automatically by creating the export rule After table processing,
which executes the global function ZAPI_SWITCH_DATA.
You can switch data manually via transaction /N/SNP/SG in the source system.

6.2.6 Differing Target Client
You can use the staging manager type C for staging in other clients to migrate data into the sta-
ging area without creating a shadow table. Data can be written to the different target client,
deleted from it, and swapped with the data in the actual target client.
The staging manager for different target clients is particularly useful for cluster and pool tables if
you want to prevent the affected tables from being converted into transparent tables during the
data switch.
A shadow client is an automatically generated three character string from AAA (0) to ZZZ
(17,576). A new shadow client is generated for each new staging target area.
6.2.6.1 Piping Data Toward Staging
You can pipe data toward staging by transferring it to the class /SNP/SG05_CL_DB_ACC_
INTERCE (DB Access Interceptor) (See "Global ZAPI Functions" on page 529).
You have to explicitly indicate the usage of differing target client mode and provide a target area
ID that corresponds to the client field.
Instantiation of DB Access Interceptor with differing client staging mode:

" Indication of differing target client mode
CALL METHOD lr_interceptor->set_clnt_staging.
NOTE
The mode differing target client supports all the writing modes (INSERT, INSERT_
ADK, INSLOG, LOGMOD, LOGADK, DELLOG, DELETE, UPDATE and MODIFY).

6.2.8 Logged ADK Insertion Mode
The insertion mode Logged ADK (LOGADK) was developed for use cases where duplicate data
records might occur and information on the inserted data records is required. This mode allows
the user to insert data without duplicates into the target table without enabling the ACCEPTING
DUPLICATE KEYS option. By separating the duplicate records and inserted data records, you
can restore the original contents of the target tables at a later time.
6.2.8.1 Log Tables
Information regarding which data records were or were not inserted is stored in staging log
areas.
Log for duplicate keys: stores all the rows that have been identified as duplicates.
Log for inserted keys: stores all the rows that have been inserted during the trans-
formation.
Log for deleted keys: stores all rows that have been identified as duplicates and have
therefore been replaced with new, modified data records.
Log for inserted keys: stores all the rows that have been inserted during a transformation.
Log for temporary keys: contains temporary data that is only used during processing.
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter537

=====PAGE 538=====
Logs are implemented as shadow tables in DDIC staging mode and as shadow clients in CLNT
mode. You can access the names of the log areas using the transaction /N/SNP/SG_
LOCATION.

6.2.8.3 Staging Deletion
The staging area deletion function is available for Logged ADK mode. Staging logs are also
deleted when you delete the staging area.
6.2.9 Restoring Deleted Data
The DELETE_LOG mode is used to delete data from the target system. You can use this mode
to undo changes or restore deleted data via a log table. You can use the report /SNP/SG05_
ROLLBACK_FROM_LOG to undo the last saved changes.
The report works for all logged write modes and also for combined write modes, e.g. MODIFY_
LOG and DELETE_LOG.
NOTE
Once a data record is written into a log table, it is neither written nor updated again. This
means that the original status which existed before writing is always restored.
6.2.9.1 Log Tables
The DELETE_LOG mode uses the following log tables:
Log for temporary keys: contains temporary data that is only used during processing
Log for deleted keys: contains the original data that has been deleted
Logs are implemented as shadow tables in DDIC staging mode and as shadow clients in CLNT
mode. You can access the names of the log areas using the report /SNP/SG05_GET_
SHADOW_TABNAME.

If you perform a staging operation, a log entry is created. You can use the log for analyses and
therefore identify and reverse malfunctions and application errors.

Creation

Delete

The log is stored in two tables that you can start using transactions /N/SNP/SG_LOG and
SE16: 
User Guide - Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Platzhalter541

=====PAGE 542=====
/SNP/SG05DDTSTAT (header table)
/SNP/SG05DDDET (detailed table – connected to the header table via foreign key)
The header table contains the following data:
Table ID (ID of the table)
Target area (ID of the target area)
Manager (staging manager type)
Data (only for one data switch)
Deletion indicator (indicates whether the table still exists)
Changer (last changed by)
Change date (modification date)
Change time (time of the change)

The option Create staging for tables creates shadow tables or registers a staging client in the
system. These actions are also performed automatically on the first write access. However, to
reduce technical runtimes and risks, they can also be created manually in advance. This dis-
plays potential errors during creation before they have an impact on any migration activities.

and Cluster Tables.
3. Select the Staging Manager type.
4. Optional: Define a unique target area ID.
NOTE
By assigning the target area ID, you can separate data within the staging. In
the case of the client staging manager (type C), a new target area ID results in
the use of a new staging client (AAA-ZZZ). In the case of the DDIC shadow
table staging manager (type D), the target area ID influences the generation of
table names for the shadow tables so that different target areas use different
shadow tables. In the case of different staging manager types (for the same tar-
get area), the different storage methods also separate the data. Data sep-
aration can be useful, for example, if you are running multiple tests
simultaneously. You can change the default value to any combination of let-
ters, numbers and symbols up to 32 characters.
