11.3.4.6.4 Performing Delta Transfers
A delta transfer transfers the data out of the collector tables from the source systems to the target
systems. The object keys are concatenated and hashed taking into account the table extensions of
all table chains for an NZD object.
Proceed as follows to perform a delta transfer:
1. Start transaction SE38.
2. In the Program field, enter the report /SNP/ZD02_DELTA_TRANSFER.
3. Click
Execute.
The window Transfer changes from source systems to target systems opens.
4. Specify a scenario.
5. Enter a name for the delta transfer.
NOTE
Enter a unique name, otherwise the system uses the timestamp and the name of
the executing user.
6. Specify which changes you want to transfer by including or excluding collector IDs, NZD
objects, source systems and target systems.
7. Optional: Adjust the package size.
8. Optional: Adjust the value for Collector package size.

=====PAGE 1039=====
1039
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
NOTE
The Collector package size defines the number of collector IDs for a transfer
package of a collector table. The lower the value, the better the packages can be
parallelized. However, this also increases the number of packages.
9. Optional: Adjust the Number of processes.
10. Click
Execute.
The delta transfer has been started.
Go to Migration > Object key transfers to access an overview of all performed delta trans-
fers.
11.3.4.6.5 Executing Delta Deletion Runs
A delta deletion run deletes data on the basis of one or more delta transfers. You can restrict the
delta deletion run to certain delta transfers.
Prerequisites
For each combination of NZD object and source system – according to which the deletion
occurs – at least one delta transfer has been successfully performed.
Proceed as follows to perform a delta deletion run:
1. Start transaction SE38.
2. In the Program field, enter the report /SNP/ZD02_RUN_DELTA_DELETION.
3. Click
Execute.
The Execute deletion run window opens.
4. Specify a scenario.
5. Enter a unique ID for the deletion run.
6. Specify which data you want to delete by including or excluding delta transfers, migration
objects, target tables, NZD objects, source systems and target systems.
7. Optional: Select the option Simulation to initially only determine how many records have
been deleted.
8. Optional: Select the option Log records to be deleted to log all records found in the protocol
table.
9. Optional: Select the option System-specific.

=====PAGE 1040=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1040
NOTE
If you clear this option, the data records are deleted across multiple systems. Dele-
tion across multiple systems means that data records are deleted even if the sys-
tem on which the data record change took place is a different system than the
system from which the data record originated.
This is especially relevant for projects where a harmonization takes place.
10. Optional: Adjust the package size.
NOTE
The package size does not equate to the number of deleted records. Because the
system deletes using object keys, it is possible for the number of deleted records
to be significantly higher than the specified package size. This relationship results
from the cardinality of the table to its root table.
11. Optional: Adjust the Number of processes.
12. Click
Execute.
The delta deletion run has been started.
Go to Migration > Deletion log to access an overview of all performed delta deletion runs.

11.3.4.7.3 Creating Artificial Changes
To test the RBNZD approach, changes that the collector can gather are necessary in order to
restrict a delta load. Because an SLT replication or another procedure is not always available in
test phases before the go-live – i.e. a procedure that initiates the trigger and therefore generates
changes for a delta load – it is possible to generate changes based on exports in the Transformation
Cockpit.
Proceed as follows to create artificial changes:
1. Start transaction SE38.

11.3.5 RBNZD Lite
RBNZD Lite is a special use case for RBNZD that you can use under certain conditions to reduce
the runtime overhead and complexity of the RBNZD procedure.
In the traditional procedure, the delta is migrated via an undo/redo mechanism, where the delta is
deleted or reset on the target system and migrated again using the original import mode (e.g.
INSERT). The idea of RBNZD Lite is not to reset the delta on the target system in the delta loads,
but to overwrite it. To do so, the delta loads are migrated using the import mode MODIFY.

=====PAGE 1046=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1046
You can adjust the configuration for RBNZD Lite per individual table. RBNZD Lite differs from the
traditional procedure concerning the following aspects:
No import logging takes place. This reduces the runtime, especially in the initial load, where
the largest amount of data is transferred.
No table extension is generated. This eliminates some of the rule base constraints, such as
the cardinality constraint that is usually responsible for issues regarding table extensions.
No protocol and versioning tables are generated.
No delta transfer and no delta deletion run are performed.
11.3.5.1 Prerequisites
Compared to the traditional procedure, the delta is not reset on the target system before the delta
load, but overwritten directly. Therefore, after a RBNZD Lite delta load, you must ensure that no
data exists that is not allowed to exist. The result must be the same as the result after a standard
delta load.
The following requirements must be met to use RBNZD Lite without errors:
No deletions are transferred in the relevant tables in the delta. Deleted data records are not
exported in the delta and are therefore not overwritten in the target. As a result, inconsistent
orphaned data records from the previous loads might remain in the target.
Changes in the delta must not lead to a change in the migration scope. If a data record was
migrated in a previous load and subsequently becomes out of scope due to a change on the
source system, the data record must be removed from the target system. This is not the case
with an RBNZD Lite delta load; the data record would be orphaned and therefore incon-
sistent.
The migration rule base must guarantee stable primary keys. If a data record was migrated in
a previous load with a specific primary key and receives a different primary key in the next
load due to a change on the source system, both data records would exist on the target sys-
tem after the RBNZD Lite delta load. The originally migrated data record is orphaned and the-
refore inconsistent.
11.3.5.2 Risks
Using the mode MODIFY during the migration involves the risk of overwriting data records
incorrectly without being noticed. Duplicates that exist within the rule base are not identified,
for example.
If the prerequisites are not met, inconsistencies can occur in the target system.

=====PAGE 1047=====
1047
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
The configuration of RBNZD Lite (e.g. the migration scope) cannot be automatically trans-
ferred to a new NZD scenario. Instead, manual steps are required that are more error-prone
than an automated procedure.
11.3.5.3 How-to
The following instructions apply when using the Transformation Cockpit as the migration engine.
RBNZD Lite can be configured for each individual table in the RBNZD scope. Proceed as follows to
configure a table for processing using RBNZD Lite:
1. Remove the table from the migration scope (see the chapter Extending the Table Scoping).
2. Set the import mode of the table in the Transformation Cockpit to MODIFY (see the chapter
Modes and Options).
3. Change the call setting of the RBNZD import logger in the global event of the Transformation
Cockpit so that the import logger for the RBNZD Lite tables is not called.
4. Optional: If you want to use the table in the entire scenario with RBNZD Lite, you can delete
existing protocol and versioning tables (see the chapter Deleting Scenarios).
NOTE
To transfer this configuration to another scenario, for example to perform a new test
migration, manual steps are required.

12.3 Data Consistency Verification
12.3.1 What is Data Consistency Verification?
Data Consistency Verification is a stand-alone software component that has been continuously
developed for over fifteen years to ensure referential integrity after data transfers and data con-
versions. It is the only software from the SAP® environment that validates all foreign keys, value
tables and domain fixed values within a few hours, even with data volumes of several terabytes.
The speed of this check is crucial in order to resume productive operation in SAP® systems after
imports or conversions and to avoid economic damage caused by data inconsistencies that only
become visible during ongoing operation. The verification reveals incomplete header tables (cus-
tomizing and master data) as well as errors caused by the data conversion or data mapping. While
evaluating these results, which are referred to as inconsistencies below, the focus is on efficiency
and transparency. This allows you to incorporate the required corrections into the rule base of the

=====PAGE 1051=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1051
migration component as quickly as possible. The results remain available after completing a project
to be able to trace the data quality in the different project phases. Since the beginning of 2019, the
integration of components for the intermediate storage of data has made it possible to perform
these checks without actually writing the converted data to the target system. Like this, the veri-
fication results can be preserved while simulating the data migration or conversion.

12.3.5 Performing the Data Consistency Verification
The transaction /N/SNP/DCV of Data Consistency Verification is used to execute check runs.
These check runs comprise performing the foreign key check (with value table check) and the
domain fixed value check. After starting a check run, multiple jobs (user-defined) are scheduled to
execute the checks. You are forwarded to the monitoring view of Data Consistency Verification.
This function can be used before and after any type of data conversion or data import. It is used to
determine the data inconsistencies caused by the corresponding process.
If a data migration takes place from one system to another, the check should be performed pre-
viously on both systems and in the target system additionally after the import. This allows you to
analyze only the inconsistencies caused by the import (see chapter Subtracting Equal Results).
You can use the Goto to access additional functions of Data Consistency Verification.

12.3.5.3.3 Checks to Be Conducted
The Data Consistency Verification enables you to execute multiple functions in a single check run
(a joint transaction). This minimizes the effort involved and produces a shorter runtime and better
load distribution, i.e. better utilization of the system to be checked. If you want to use different work-
lists for the various check functions, you must use several variants and transactions.
Domain
Fixed
Value
Check
This checks domain fixed values in tables that result from the selection. The field values
of a table are checked according to the domain assigned to the data element. If a field
value is out of the value range of the domain, this is regarded as an error.
Value
table
Value tables are defined for domains. The content of table fields that are assigned to
the domain via their data element should correspond to one of the values in the value

=====PAGE 1060=====
1060
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
check
table. This means that the value table check consists of matching individual table field
values against a value table. In this sense, it is a foreign key check against a value
table that is defined by the domain. As opposed to the foreign key check, it consists of
only one check field and is therefore less extensive and less sensitive. However, you
can also perform the value table check on table fields that do not have a foreign key
and therefore use it on significantly more data.
NOTE
In a value table check, fields that are part of a foreign key check (with mul-
tiple fields) are not included in the value table check. This avoids unne-
cessary executions of incompletely defined foreign key relationships. It is
always applied and cannot be disabled.
Foreign
Key
Check
Foreign keys are defined from one table to another table – known as the check table. The
table relationship contained in the foreign key consists of one or more fields. If there is no
exact match between the combined fields of the foreign key relationship in the check
table, the foreign key check fails.

You can evaluate migrated results on the control system with DCV_RESULTS or further process

12.3.5.3.5 Options to Limit Space, Memory Consumption and Runtime
Change
runtime para-
meters
WARNING
Change runtime parameters only in exceptional cases or in connection
with a support case. Changing the runtime parameters can result in
excessively long runtimes, extremely high consumption of the database
memory, process terminations and unreliable check results.
The default values provide an optimal balance between the quality of the results
and the execution time and memory requirements. Therefore, only change these
values if you have extensive knowledge of the application.
Restricting
Inconsistent
Values
This restricts the number of inconsistent values found by the individual checks.
By default, the Limit inconsistent values option is enabled and set to 100,000 val-
ues in the field Max. no. of saved values. If the specified value is reached, the
system no longer checks domain fixed values, value tables, or foreign keys.
However, other checks within the table or other check types for the same column
can be continued. You can use this option to reduce the number of values stored
by the data consistency verification and thus shorten the check runtime and
reduce the memory requirements. Checks that are terminated on the basis of this
criterion cannot be used in subtractions. We recommend that you evaluate ter-
minated checks separately in the results evaluation by selecting the status A.

=====PAGE 1062=====
1062
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
NOTE
Even a limited number of inconsistent values can lead to duplicates
when writing to the database if the maximum buffer size is exceeded.
Therefore, the number of stored values may be below the limit, espe-
cially if the limiting value is higher than 150,000.
Expensive
Checks
Expensive checks are checks of foreign keys or value tables with more than
100,000 data records. These checks lead to an individual selection against the
respective check table for each checked value or value combination of a foreign
key. Checks of domain fixed values or value tables with less than 100,000 data
records, on the other hand, are buffered. The following options for performing
expensive checks are available:
Fully perform w/o limitation.
Do not conduct at all.
Perform expensive checks with a Max. no. of successful checks that you
define in the field Successful checks (wo. error).
Limit overall
checked val-
ues
You can use this option to limit the number of value combinations checked per table.
Select the option Value pairs per table to specify a maximum number. The default
value is 100,000,000.
Skip most
runtime-
expensive
checks
With this option, you can skip the most runtime-expensive checks. It is enabled
by default. It can be disabled in the Options area to limit storage space, memory
consumption and runtime.
The most runtime-expensive value table checks are those for values where the
target field is not the first field (after the client) and not the first field in a sec-
ondary index of the value table. In addition, the value table contains more than
100,000 values.
Replace VTC
with FKC
Enabling this option can shorten the runtime. Value table checks are not executed if
they are identical to the check tables for foreign keys. However, this can result in
fewer identified inconsistencies because the check is already included in the foreign
key check.
Convert and
save values
If this option is enabled, results imported from other systems will be displayed cor-
rectly on the control system. This means that the values are displayed without lead-

=====PAGE 1063=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1063
ing zeros or blank spaces. The conversion has little impact on performance. The con-
version is enabled by default.

12.3.5.3.6.4 Selection by organizational units
In this area you can select values of organizational units that you want to include in the check. Data
records that are not included in the selected value range are not taken into account. This reduces
the runtime and irrelevant inconsistencies.
Note that these selections only affect tables in which the specified organizational units are
included. Dependent tables are not restricted. This does not remove any tables from the worklist in
which no organizational selections can be made. Different organizational selections are connected
by an OR link. Consequently, the data is checked if it is included in an organizational selection or if
an organizational selection cannot be made in the table.
12.3.5.3.6.5 Selection by filters
By using filters during a test run, you can reduce the memory requirements and the runtime.
NOTE
The filter is used to exclude irrelevant inconsistencies for the Data Consistency Veri-
fication results. The Filter field is filled with the values 9000000 and 9000001 in the
Exclude Single Values tab by default.
You can either include filters, in which case the worklist only contains checks that match the filter,
or exclude them, in which case the worklist does not contain checks that match the filter.

=====PAGE 1067=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1067
EXAMPLE
You can create a filter for checks with inconsistencies that were checked during the test
cycle and are irrelevant or will not be corrected. By filtering according to these checks
during a test run, you can avoid unnecessary runtimes and data generation.
Filters that are used for starting the DCV run only affect the worklist. They are not applied to field
values from checks or domains. If you want to exclude single values from the check result, you
must specify the relevant filters again in the selection in the results evaluation. Note that field val-
ues from checks or domains that are in a filter do not automatically include the corresponding
checks or domains in DCV runs when they are specified at the start of the transaction. Field values
in filters are completely ignored when DCV runs are started.
12.3.5.3.6.6 Settings for data from staging (Staging Framework)

Checking data in staging areas has the advantage that only the imported data is checked. This
reduces the runtime and increases the clarity of the results and data already contained in the target
system, so that test migrations can be repeated.
NOTE
The SQLScript engine of Data Consistency Verification does not support the staging
framework.

12.3.5.4 Expensive Checks
Expensive checks are value table checks with more than 100,000 values and foreign key checks.
There are options that enable special treatment for expensive checks and therefore significantly
reduce the program runtime.
The check procedure is terminated by default if one million checks are successfully performed
without detecting new inconsistencies. You can configure the number of successful checks.

=====PAGE 1070=====
1070
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
NOTE
If you select this option, the configurable number of successful checks must run without
being interrupted by unsuccessful checks. Only then will the relevant check be ter-
minated – under the assumption that no (or no more) inconsistent values will be found
after such a large number of successful checks.
Additional information on expensive checks:
It is possible to forego expensive checks completely. This means that foreign key checks are
not performed at all. Any value table checks with more values than the specified limit are not
performed.
Expensive checks cannot be aborted. This means that no restrictions are applied. A complete
check is always performed.
Discrete pairs of field values determined from the tables to be checked are sorted in descending
order. This usually ensures that new values (imported data) are checked first.
There is a configurable number of checked value pairs. Once this number is exceeded, the check of
the respective table is aborted. It makes no difference whether or not inconsistencies were found in
the table up to that point. When the read procedure is terminated, all checks on the relevant table
finish at the same time.
An odd parameter value is rounded up to a data block size of 5,000. The default setting is 100,000
value pairs. Without this restriction, checks of individual tables can take a very long time. After
approx. 24 hours, the probability of process terminations increases due to limitations on long-run-
ning database transactions.
12.3.5.5 Selecting Organizational Units
As part of Data Consistency Verification runs, you can limit the scope of checked data by selecting
organizational units. The organizational units include company codes (BUKRS), plants (WERKS)
and purchasing organizations (EKORG). The organizational units can be used to reduce the overall
runtime of the data consistency verification. In order to optimally reduce the runtime, all available
organizational units should be used. It is not recommended to restrict the selection to table entries
for a specific organizational unit.

=====PAGE 1071=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1071
WARNING
By selecting organizational units, it is possible that some data records from inter-
company business transactions are not checked. The acceptability of this for a project
should be evaluated based on the scenario scope and the intercompany check per-
formed with transaction /N/SNP/CW_INTERCOMPANY. It is usually not necessary to
check every single data record to find all inconsistencies. Limitations of organizational
units are usually a good compromise between the runtime check and the completeness
of results.
Proceed as follows to perform a selection according to organizational units: 
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/DCV.

3. Enter the value of the desired organizational unit for which you want to restrict the scope of
the data consistency verification.
NOTE

selection for company code 1000 and you enter a selection for plant 2000, the
selection will search for entries that have either values for company code 1000
“OR” plant 2000.
4. Enter values in the fields PERSA and EINRI to limit the amount of data checked.
5. Specify the fiscal year.
6. Optional: Select the option Display org. table fields to check and adjust the selection of
organizational units before the DCV run.
7. To provide the organizational units from a TC scenario automatically, open the area Selec-
tion by Transformation Cockpit (Tc) rulesets.
NOTE
For this procedure, the area Selection by organizational units must be empty. At
least one TC scenario with selections or mappings must be available.
8. In the Central system (RFC) field, select an RFC Verbindung.

(transaction /N/SNP/DCV_MONITOR) to also display checks for which no inconsistencies were
found.
In general, a DCV transaction that is relevant for the final evaluation will result from the subtraction
of DCV transactions.
You can use the Goto to access additional functions of Data Consistency Verification.

the authorization role.

12.3.7.1 Basic Concepts
12.3.7.1.1 Data Retention in a Control System
We recommend storing the results of Data Consistency Verification in a central system (the control
system) over the course of the project and maybe beyond. This allows you to compare the results
across multiple project phases, for example via transaction /N/SNP/DCV_SUMMARY. This
approach is used to document a project and includes assessments and inconsistencies. You can
also add and use comments and filters across multiple project phases.
NOTE
The program does not currently support the transfer of comments, filters and assess-
ments from one system to another or the synchronization of such metadata.
12.3.7.1.2 Evaluating Inconsistencies
You can assign different assessments to the checks of individual table fields, checks of entire
domains, and single values of domains and checks.
Assessments are only saved for checks and check values. An assessment that you set for a
domain also applies to all checks of this domain. This is also true for the assessment of domain val-
ues. The assessment of a domain value is passed to the same value in all checks.
If assessments of the same domain values are incomplete or were performed differently in the vari-
ous checks in which the value occurs, a corresponding status appears in the domain value view.
The same applies to domains, tables and data objects if the underlying checks or check values are
incomplete or evaluated differently.

=====PAGE 1082=====
1082
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
If all checks of the transaction were evaluated directly or indirectly via domains and single values,
the whole transaction is considered to be evaluated and the results evaluation is considered to be
complete.
For the assessment of inconsistencies, the user name is stored. Such an assessment is therefore
considered to be a sign-off. The user name and the terminal used can be displayed in the domain
view, domain value view, check view and check value view. In the domain view and the domain
value view, these columns are only filled if the assessment was performed from within the respect-
ive view, but not from the check view or check value view.
You can add comments to assessments if necessary.
This allows for more transparency, as users can see whether the assessment was completed as
well as check the progress status and the qualitative result. This process helps to avoid incon-
sistencies that are checked more than once due to overlapping work packages.
12.3.7.1.3 Comments for Inconsistencies
In Data Consistency Verification, you can add comments to checks, tables, data objects, incon-
sistent domain values and inconsistent field values. These comments are independent of DCV
transactions. This means that you can use comments to transmit information to other departments,
project cycles and also projects within the system.
Comments are visible globally and can be modified at any time by any user. Currently, there is no
change history available, and comments are still posted anonymously.
For integration with Kyano Mission Control, the execution and data retention must take place in the
control system.
12.3.7.1.4 Filtering Inconsistencies
You can add domains, checks, domain values and single values from checks to filters and give
them a description.
You can then use this filter to execute new DCV runs, for monitoring and evaluation purposes, and
to export results. You can include or exclude each individual filter. Filters, like comments, are inde-
pendent of transactions.

=====PAGE 1083=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1083
You can use filters for various purposes, for example to transfer an assessment from one trans-
action to another, to set up worklists for module teams, or to exclude certain table fields that do not
need to be checked again.
The views in the evaluation are updated when content is added to or removed from the filters. This
means that rows disappear from the views when you add them to an excluded filter or remove them
from all included filters.
12.3.7.1.5 Create DCV Run Backup Before Checking Again
You can use this function to create a backup of a DCV run before performing a check again. This
provides you with a copy of the original inconsistencies found and allows you to check the original
run at any time.
Proceed as follows to create a DCV run backup:
1. Start transaction /SNP/DCV_RESULTS.
The window SNP Data Consistency Verification: Evaluate results opens.
2. In the Transaction field, select a run.
3. In the section Please select the results evaluation entry view, select the Checks option.
4. Click
Execute.
The Aggregated by checks table opens.
5. Select the desired results. To do so, click the first column from the left-hand side.
6. Click Check again.
The window Parameters for checking again opens.
7. Enable the option Create DCV run backup before checking again.
8. Click Check again.
The DCV run backup is created and can be displayed using transaction /SNP/DCV_
RESULTS.
12.3.7.1.6 Rechecking Inconsistencies
In the check view and in the domain view, you can recheck selected checks for inconsistencies or
recheck all checks for selected domains for inconsistencies.

that do not appear in the check results are added. Previously subtracted transactions are taken into
account – previously subtracted values are not added again.

During the evaluation, you can switch between the initial views at any time by clicking the cor-

However, you can only select the data object view if the selected transaction number was started
by specifying a scenario in the Transformation Cockpit.
In addition, there are three views that you cannot use for the initial view. Instead, you can only
access them through the initial views:
The Check value view displays the inconsistent values of a check. You can access this view
by double-clicking a check.
The Exemplary inconsistent data records view displays entire data records that contain
inconsistent values. You can access this view by double-clicking a value in the check value

=====PAGE 1086=====
1086
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
view. After gathering exemplary inconsistent data records, you can also access this view by
clicking Examples in the check value view. It then displays examples for all inconsistent val-
ues from the check instead of just one value.
The Domain value view displays inconsistent domain values. You can access it by double-
clicking a domain in the domain view. Double-click a domain value to open the check view
again. Here, only checks are displayed in which the corresponding domain value was found.
When you double-click a check, the check value view is skipped (this view would only show
the selected domain value), and the exemplary inconsistent data records are directly dis-
played.
Further interaction between the views starts when you double-click a data object or a table in the
respective view. The check view opens and only displays checks for the selected data object or
selected table.
This selection on a table or data object remains, even if you switch to another view. This means that
all domains for a data object or a table can be displayed, as well as all data objects for a table or all
tables for a data object. You can remove a selection by double-clicking another table or data object
or by navigating backwards via F3.
The Goto menu is available in all views of the results evaluation, allowing you to jump to other sub-
areas of Data Consistency Verification.
12.3.7.4 Transferring Assessments
You can transfer assessments of inconsistencies between program runs. You can find more inform-
ation in the Transferring Assessments chapter.
12.3.7.5 View of Checks
In the checks view, all performed checks are displayed according to the initial selection for the res-
ults evaluation. Checks are performed for table fields. You can perform a foreign key check and a
value table check or a domain fixed value check for a table field. This means that a maximum of two
rows per table field and DCV transaction are displayed in this view.

4. Click
Execute.
The worklist is selected.
5. Start transaction /N/SNP/DCV_RESULTS.

7. Click
Execute.

eign key definitions originate from.

12.3.7.7 View-specific Functions
12.3.7.7.1 View of Completed Checks
Each check has a primary table field for which the check was performed. In the case of the domain
value check and value table check, the check is performed exclusively for data from this one field. If
a foreign key is defined for a table field, the foreign key can also contain other table fields – and will
do in most cases. These other field names are listed within the Checks view in the Checked fields
column. A foreign key check is performed for the combination of values from these fields. A value
could itself be consistent but then prove to be inconsistent when checked in combination with other
values.
Click Assess to assess whether a transaction is correct or incorrect.

=====PAGE 1092=====
1092
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
The Missing leading zeros column shows in which domain at least one inconsistency exists that
contains a missing leading zero.
12.3.7.7.2 View of Checked Field Values
In the field value view, the first column DB view displays the checked data as it is stored in the data-
base. For foreign key checks, this column contains concatenated field values separated by a pipe
symbol.
When additional columns are created, they are correctly typed, so that data is displayed as it would
appear in the application. Such typed columns also contain the descriptive texts from the relevant
data elements in their header. For the value table check and domain fixed value check, there is only
one typed column. For the foreign key check, there can be multiple typed columns.
If the transaction /N/SNP/DCV has been migrated from another system, typed columns are not dis-
played. This is because the original data elements might not exist locally.
NOTE
You can evaluate individual field values.
12.3.7.7.3 View of Inconsistent Data Records
Double-click a value in the view of the checked field values to select the inconsistent data records
from among the selected data records. This is only possible in the local system and does not take
the staging framework into account. The domain view summarizes domains across multiple trans-
actions.
Once you have double-clicked the value, a prompt appears if the checked table contains more than
500,000 data records. The prompt asks whether you want to continue the task or to display only the
inconsistent data records found in the first 500,000 data records of the checked table.
Another prompt appears if 200 example data records with a specific inconsistent value have been
found, because this is usually enough for verifications.
If you decide to continue the selection in both cases, only then will the system try to load all incon-
sistent data records from the checked table for the selected value. This might lead to a memory
overflow and very long runtimes.
Click Recheck to recheck inconsistent data records.

=====PAGE 1093=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1093
12.3.7.7.4 View of Checked Domains
The Domains view allows you to aggregate the results of the data consistency verification accord-
ing to domains. This is useful because many conversions are defined at the domain level, and
domains are checked multiple times for different tables.
Click Assess to assess whether a transaction is correct or incorrect.
The Missing leading zeros column shows in which domain at least one inconsistency exists that
contains a missing leading zero.
WARNING
You cannot evaluate foreign key check results via the view of checked domains. This is
because each inconsistent value of a foreign key check always consists of a con-
catenation of values of all fields within a foreign key definition. You can see which of the
fields caused the foreign key check to abort. The values from the foreign key check res-
ults are linked to their respective domains and displayed in the domain view. However,
when viewing an individual value, you cannot obtain valid information about the entire
foreign key. Even if you correct the value in question, this does not mean that the entire
foreign key is correct. It is possible that multiple fields were inconsistent and therefore
that the foreign key check as a whole will still fail.
Use the views Checks and Check value to evaluate foreign keys. The Checks view con-
tains the Checked domains column, which allows you to filter out all foreign key checks
for a domain. Check them individually because they might be inconsistent due to other
domains.

=====PAGE 1094=====
1094
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
NOTE
You can evaluate individual check values and domain values in the results of the data
consistency verification. Furthermore, the assessment of check values/domain values
affects the assessment of checks/domains by marking them as “Partially assessed” if
some values are identical. The remainder is marked as “Not assessed” or as “Mixed
assessment” if there are at least two different assessment statuses (other than “Not
assessed”).
If all check values/domain values are assessed identically, an assessment for the entire
check/domain is created. This assessment is displayed just like in situations where the
entire check/domain is assessed. Note that the assessment of the check/domain over-
writes the assessment of the individual values.
12.3.7.7.5 View of Domain Values
Double-click a value in the view of the checked domains to select the inconsistent values in this
domain. The first column of the domain value view displays the data in an unconverted database
format. If transaction /N/SNP/DCV has not been migrated, there is a second column in which the
domain values are displayed as they would appear in the application.
The three columns Fixed value check, Value table check and Foreign key check indicate the
check for which a domain value was found. If it was only found in a foreign key check and not in a
value table check, the inconsistency only occurs in combination with values from other values. You
can create and include a filter in order to find the checks that a domain value or domain belongs to.
Double-clicking a domain value takes you to the Aggregated by checks view. However, this view
only filters according to the checks in which the domain value occurred. Depending on the value in
the Type of check column, another double-click takes you to the following views:
The Foreign key check value to the field value view
The Value table check value to the view of the examples per unique error value
The value Domain fixed value check to the view of the examples per unique error value

12.3.7.9.1 Gathering Exemplary Inconsistent Data Records
This chapter describes how to gather examples of inconsistent records from all checked table for a
transaction of Data Consistency Verification. You can gather the examples via RFC from a remote
system.
We recommend the procedure that is provided in Kyano Mission Control: Starting exemplary data
records from a central control system after the substraction(s) for the final results.
This way, exemplary inconsistent data records are transferred to the central system and doc-
umented there, regardless of whether the satellite system still exists or not.
NOTE
Significantly increased values for Max. saved examples or Examples per value can
lead to long runtimes and reduce the available database storage.
Prerequisites
A DCV transaction has been created by a check run or a subtraction.
Proceed as follows to gather examples of data records:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/DCV_EXAMPLES.
NOTE
Alternatively, you can open the window via the menu Goto > Run control >
Gather examples.
2. The window Data Consistency Verification: Gathering of exemplary records opens.
3. Specify the short transaction no..
4. Specify the number of processes.
5. In the Max. saved examples field, specify the number of examples gathered per check.
6. Specify the number of examples per value gathered in the check.
7. Click
Execute.
The examples of inconsistent records have been gathered for the selected transaction. A
message appears in the lower window.

12.3.10 View-specific Functions
12.3.10.1 View of Completed Checks
Each check has a primary table field for which the check was performed. In the case of the domain
value check and value table check, the check is performed exclusively for data from this one field. If
a foreign key is defined for a table field, the foreign key can also contain other table fields – and will
do in most cases. These other field names are listed within the Checks view in the Checked fields
column. A foreign key check is performed for the combination of values from these fields. A value
could itself be consistent but then prove to be inconsistent when checked in combination with other
values.
Click Assess to assess whether a transaction is correct or incorrect.

=====PAGE 1113=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1113
The Missing leading zeros column shows in which domain at least one inconsistency exists that
contains a missing leading zero.
12.3.10.2 View of Checked Field Values
In the field value view, the first column DB view displays the checked data as it is stored in the data-
base. For foreign key checks, this column contains concatenated field values separated by a pipe
symbol.
When additional columns are created, they are correctly typed, so that data is displayed as it would
appear in the application. Such typed columns also contain the descriptive texts from the relevant
data elements in their header. For the value table check and domain fixed value check, there is only
one typed column. For the foreign key check, there can be multiple typed columns.
If the transaction /N/SNP/DCV has been migrated from another system, typed columns are not dis-
played. This is because the original data elements might not exist locally.
NOTE
You can evaluate individual field values.
12.3.10.3 View of Inconsistent Data Records
Double-click a value in the view of the checked field values to select the inconsistent data records
from among the selected data records. This is only possible in the local system and does not take
the staging framework into account. The domain view summarizes domains across multiple trans-
actions.
Once you have double-clicked the value, a prompt appears if the checked table contains more than
500,000 data records. The prompt asks whether you want to continue the task or to display only the
inconsistent data records found in the first 500,000 data records of the checked table.
Another prompt appears if 200 example data records with a specific inconsistent value have been
found, because this is usually enough for verifications.
If you decide to continue the selection in both cases, only then will the system try to load all incon-
sistent data records from the checked table for the selected value. This might lead to a memory
overflow and very long runtimes.
Click Recheck to recheck inconsistent data records.

=====PAGE 1114=====
1114
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
12.3.10.4 View of Checked Domains
The Domains view allows you to aggregate the results of the data consistency verification accord-
ing to domains. This is useful because many conversions are defined at the domain level, and
domains are checked multiple times for different tables.
Click Assess to assess whether a transaction is correct or incorrect.
The Missing leading zeros column shows in which domain at least one inconsistency exists that
contains a missing leading zero.
WARNING
You cannot evaluate foreign key check results via the view of checked domains. This is
because each inconsistent value of a foreign key check always consists of a con-
catenation of values of all fields within a foreign key definition. You can see which of the
fields caused the foreign key check to abort. The values from the foreign key check res-
ults are linked to their respective domains and displayed in the domain view. However,
when viewing an individual value, you cannot obtain valid information about the entire
foreign key. Even if you correct the value in question, this does not mean that the entire
foreign key is correct. It is possible that multiple fields were inconsistent and therefore
that the foreign key check as a whole will still fail.
Use the views Checks and Check value to evaluate foreign keys. The Checks view con-
tains the Checked domains column, which allows you to filter out all foreign key checks
for a domain. Check them individually because they might be inconsistent due to other
domains.

12.3.13 Subtracting Equal Results
You can use this function to subtract the results of transactions of a data consistency verification
from each other. One of the transactions is defined as a minuend and the other one as a sub-
trahend. The result, i.e. the difference, is saved as a separate new transaction. You can use all func-
tions for this new transaction, including further subtractions.
The subtraction of result sets in Data Consistency Verification is used to filter out inconsistencies
that are irrelevant for the evaluation. If you use Kyano Mission Control to manage the project, this
also ensures that the relevant steps are carried out in the correct sequence.

=====PAGE 1119=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1119
In general, the results of a check run of DCV on a system contain all inconsistencies that are part of
the scope of the check run. However, the sum of all inconsistencies on the system is usually not rel-
evant for the current project. In the case of data imports and conversions, the focus is on identifying
the inconsistencies that were caused by or imported during the conversion. In order to limit the res-
ult set to these inconsistencies, a DCV check run is executed before and after the conversion or
data import.
The run executed after the import serves as the minuend for the subtraction and the preceding run
as the subtrahend. The result (difference) represents the number of imported inconsistencies or
those caused by the conversion. If an SAP source system exists from which the data was imported,
it is also possible to transfer and subtract this data. This allows you to narrow down the number of
imported inconsistencies to only newly created inconsistencies.
NOTE
If the transaction of the subtrahend is newer than the transaction of the minuend, the
user must confirm this in a separate window. This confirmation ensures that no trans-
actions have been confused with one another.
Prerequisites
There are two check transactions with equal selections.
Proceed as follows to subtract equal results:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/DCV_SUBTRACT.
The window SNP DCV: Subtraction of results from each other opens.
2. In the field From this set of results, specify the transaction from which you want to subtract
the results.
3. In the field Remove equal results of, specify the transaction to be subtracted.
4. In the area Remove checks, if they are identical, enable one of the following options:
a. Inconsistent field values to subtract individual inconsistent values if they are identical.
This option also determines cases where the same number but different values are
inconsistent. The result is saved as a new transaction.
b. Inconsistent domain values to subtract inconsistent values if they exist for the same
domain. This type of subtraction delivers results with a smaller scope than a sub-
traction at the field value level. This is particularly evident if the scope of the check runs
varies because the checked fields were not the same, for example due to differing
releases, the use of views or execution problems. You can also subtract previously

=====PAGE 1120=====
1120
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
existing inconsistencies if the data was transferred to other tables (e.g. ACDOCA) via
an S/4HANA migration, for example.
5. Optional: Enable the option Use subtrahend worklist to consider only checks that are part of
the worklist of the subtracting transaction.
NOTE
You can use this option, for example, if you only want to look at checks that
already exist in a lower release.
6. Optional: Disable the option Exclude from result completely if you do not want to exclude
checks from the final result that terminate after the maximum number of inconsistent values
has been reached. These results are excluded by default because the subtraction cannot be
applied to them in a reliable manner. If they are not excluded, inconsistencies that should
have been subtracted can occur in the difference.
NOTE
There are numerous options for reducing runtime and memory requirements that
can cause checks to terminate. Terminated checks should be evaluated sep-
arately in the respective check results.
If one of the two checks involved was terminated due to reaching the limit of the
inconsistent values stored, the subtraction can be incomplete or, in rare cases, it
is possible that too many results were subtracted. A conclusive assessment is not
possible because, if a termination occurs, neither the number of inconsistent val-
ues nor all individual inconsistent values are known.
7. Optional: Enable the Automatically gather examples option.
NOTE
With this option, exemplary data records of inconsistent values are determined,
transferred and stored directly after the subtraction. This is useful for doc-
umentation purposes and to improve the response times in the evaluation when
accessing exemplary inconsistent data records. It does not increase the runtime
of the subtraction. The runtime is determined in a separately scheduled job that is
executed subsequently.

=====PAGE 1121=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1121
8. Optional: Enable the Apply mappings option.
a. Specify the desired scenario ID of the Transformation Cockpit for the mapping.
b. Specify the system alias for the mapping.
NOTE
Assignments that contain this system alias are included in the scope in case
assignments are applied.
NOTE
If you use the parameter Apply mappings, the DCV transaction that is specified
as the subtrahend will be saved in a new DCV transaction. In this new transaction,
the mapping rules from the scenario are applied to the inconsistent field values,
which is then subtracted from the minuend transaction. You can use this pro-
cedure to subtract inconsistencies that already existed before the migration, even
if they have been converted. In addition to subtractions, you can also apply map-
ping rules to a DCV transaction by using transaction /N/SNP/DCV_MAP.
9. Click
Execute.
The subtraction has been started.
12.3.13.1 Use Cases
The following use cases describe how subtraction can be used to minimize the resulting incon-
sistencies found to the project-related results.
12.3.13.1.1 Conversion
Before and after a conversion within a system, a data consistency verification is performed. The res-
ults of the check before conversion are subtracted from the results after conversion. Only incon-
sistencies that were determined during the conversion are listed.
12.3.13.1.2 Migration
A foreign key check is performed on the source and target systems before the import. After the
import into the target system, a last third data consistency verification run is performed and the two
previous transactions are subtracted. We recommend that you first subtract the inconsistencies
from the target system before the import and then subtract the inconsistencies from this result from

=====PAGE 1122=====
1122
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
the source system. The intermediate result contains all inconsistencies in the imported data, the
final result contains all inconsistencies in the imported data that did not previously exist in the
source system.
NOTE
Not all inconsistencies found by the data consistency verification lead to problems. Even
with an unadjusted, standard operation of an SAP® system, data is created in violation
of foreign key restrictions, and in many cases this is not a problem for the application
that uses such data.
NOTE
Assessments are also migrated during the migration.
12.3.13.2 Properties
As with other selection screens, all selections behave in such a way that they restrict one another –
they are not additive.
From this set of
results
The transaction from which the results are to be subtracted.
Remove equal
results of
The transaction to be subtracted.
Number of
inconsistent
values
This function is based on the performed checks. Checks are removed from the
final result if there was an equal number of inconsistent values.
This can only lead to a useful result during a conversion. The advantage of this
option lies exclusively in the faster subtraction runtime, since single values are
not taken into account. Use this function only in time-critical situations. The res-
ults of such a subtraction cannot be saved and further processed. This value
view shows all values of the minuend transaction for checks with an unequal
number of inconsistent values.
Inconsistent
field values
This is the standard subtraction function that works on the basis of the individual
inconsistent values. Individual inconsistent field values are subtracted if they are
identical. This mode also identifies cases where the same number but different val-
ues are inconsistent. The transaction resulting from the difference between min-

=====PAGE 1123=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1123
uend and subtrahend lists the inconsistent values correctly and is saved as a new
transaction.
Inconsistent
domain values
This is the subtraction function that works on the basis of the inconsistent
domain values. Checks are removed if they have the same domain and check
value. This allows for a smaller and in some cases more meaningful summary of
inconsistencies, as well as less effort in evaluating the inconsistencies.
NOTE
When evaluating foreign key checks (FKC), subtractions take into
account the full concatenated value for the entire FKC. Only if this
total value is identical, it will be removed for a domain. Therefore, it
is possible that some checks are still displayed after subtraction,
even if the domains are identical.
Use sub-
trahend work-
list
Checks that are not in the worklist of the subtracted transaction are also com-
pletely subtracted. This allows you to subtract the results of a lower SAP®
release from those of a higher release. Checks that did not exist in the lower
release are automatically excluded.
To remove irrelevant inconsistencies from the final data consistency verification
results of the target system, we recommend that you subtract results from the
source and target systems before the import, unless a data consistency veri-
fication transaction from before the import is not available.
Exclude from
result com-
pletely
All checks that terminated in the minuend or subtrahend transaction will also be
subtracted from the final result.
The maximum limit for searching for inconsistent values is 100,000 values by
default. This limit is enabled by default to avoid unnecessary runtime and space
requirements. This means that it cannot be determined with certainty whether
exactly the same values were inconsistent in two transactions. Even if the first
100,000 inconsistent values are identical, there may still be different incon-
sistent values that were not found during the check due to the restriction. The
subtraction therefore does not provide valid information for terminated checks.
For this reason, they are excluded from the subtraction results by default, even
if this does not take into account possible inconsistencies.

=====PAGE 1124=====
1124
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
Automatically
gather
examples
Once the transaction has been executed, you can start the collection of examples
of inconsistent data records automatically.
12.3.13.3 Applying Mappings to Inconsistencies
You can use this function to apply mappings that are defined in Transformation Cockpit. To apply
the mappings, the existing DCV run is migrated to a new DCV transaction by changing the cor-
responding field values. A distinction is made between two types of mapping:
It is a single mapping if the mapping scenario consists of a source field and a target field and
both are assigned the same domain.
It is a multiple mapping if there are multiple fields on the source and target and the target
domains are a subset of the source domains.
Prerequisites
Scenarios and mappings have been created via /N/SNP/TC.
A DCV transaction has been created.
Proceed as follows to apply mappings to inconsistencies:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/DCV_MAP.
The window Data Consistency Verification: Apply mappings to inconsistencies opens.
2. Enter a transaction ID.
3. Enter a scenario ID.
4. Click
Execute.

12.3.17 Reusing Worklists
This chapter describes how to reuse an already performed data consistency verification. A new
transaction based on the data of the old one is then created. Reusing a worklist allows you to start
transaction /N/SNP/DCV more quickly.
Transaction /N/SNP/DCV_REUSE allows you to reuse a previously created worklist. This allows
you to reduce the time required to start the check. You can call such a worklist from a performed
transaction or a transaction started with the option Only save worklist. It is irrelevant whether the
transaction has been completed or canceled.
Reusing a worklist is only useful if you want to minimize the runtime and if the list of necessary
checks is relatively large (e.g. check of an entire system). The process does not replace the use
and management of report variants for transaction /N/SNP/DCV.
NOTE
We do not recommend using worklists older than a few weeks. DDIC settings can
change between the creation and reuse in the system. This may cause that individual
checks are no longer included in the new transaction and the process terminates if
checks can no longer be executed. Reusing worklists does not take into account
changes to CE or TC rule bases.
Proceed as follows to reuse a worklist:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/DCV_REUSE.
The window Data Consistency Verification: Reuse worklist opens.

12.3.19 General Information on the Completeness of Data Con-
sistency Verification
This chapter answers the question of whether Data Consistency Verification “checks everything” or
“checks completely” and also whether it “finds everything”.

=====PAGE 1141=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1141
Experience from hundreds of projects over many years has shown that there are no reports of
inconsistencies that Data Consistency Verification did not find but should have found according to
the defined specification (known as false negatives). In addition, DCV has two independent
engines written in different programming languages, whose results are regularly compared and are
identical. Therefore, DCV arrives at the same result in two different ways.
Certain technical compromises are necessary to ensure that Data Consistency Verification checks
have optimal runtimes. In test cycles, regular runtimes of under 48 hours are feasible – ideally with a
maximum of 12 hours. If you want to use Data Consistency Verification within a go-live, the feasible
runtimes are also much shorter. During projects, if these runtimes were not adhered to or if indi-
vidual background processes were aborted, then the verification would not be used. It is important
to ensure the best possible ratio between the runtime of the checks and the results they deliver.
DCV performs data checks multiple times. The data inconsistencies found are mainly due to miss-
ing entries in customizing and master data. However, it checks the references from the transaction
data in particular. This means that dependent tables are checked against header tables. The same
domain value can be missing or shown as missing in many dependent tables. Regarding the result
of DCV, it is usually sufficient to note that missing values do exist for a domain. The respective
domains are checked against many hundreds of tables. The same values in many data records can
also occur multiple times. For example, it is possible that, in one hundred million records, you only
need to check twelve unique values in one column. However, it is also possible for a unique column
to contain millions of different values. In this case, you do not need to check all the inconsistent val-
ues individually. Only a few examples are necessary in order to identify the cause of the incon-
sistencies in the domain.
The redundancy in the checks enables content-related performance optimizations in order to
achieve the required short runtimes beyond the purely technical optimizations. A check is only abor-
ted if continuing to execute it no longer makes sense because its content is not important enough to
make the long runtime worthwhile. It is assumed that either enough values have already been iden-
tified for the domains checked or that additional values will be found in other tables.
As described in other chapters of the documentation, the following content-related restrictions are
implemented:
Only a limited number of inconsistent values are stored (100,000 by default).
Without this restriction, the runtime, the required database space for the results, and
the runtime of the downstream results processing would all increase significantly.
However, this restriction has serious implications: Without complete inconsistent

=====PAGE 1142=====
1142
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
values, the subtraction of results fundamentally cannot work. By default, checks that
exceed the maximum stored inconsistent values are no longer taken into account in the
subtraction result (from the difference). We recommend checking aborted checks with
the status A and the abort reason I separately in the Data Consistency Verification mon-
itor or in the results evaluation (DCV result that was determined after the data import on
the target side) before the subtraction.
A table is only checked up to a certain number of combinations of values to be checked (100
million by default).
Especially for larger tables, this number corresponds to the data records in the table.
Checks that have been aborted in this way are handled normally in the results eval-
uation. It is assumed that, after 100 million value combinations, all or at least suf-
ficiently many inconsistent values have been found. Note that the AnyDB engine of
DCV tries to check new data records first.
Column checks are terminated after a certain number of checks in which no new inconsistent
values were found (after one million by default).
This option is only supported by the AnyDB engine. Due to its architecture, the
SAP® S/4HANA engine cannot abort checks based on this criterion. In addition, the
only checks that are aborted are those in which the values from the tables being
checked against cannot be buffered. These are foreign key checks and value table
checks with more than 100,000 different values. Results from these aborted checks are
processed without restriction. The assumption is that all inconsistent values have been
found. Here, it is relevant that the AnyDB engine tries to check new data records first.
Skip the most runtime expensive value table checks (enabled by default).
If this option is enabled, for value table checks that are not buffered due to over
100,000 values existing in the value table, the application checks whether the field in
question in the check table is the first field in the primary key of the table, or whether a
secondary index exists on the field. If this is not the case, the runtime of such a check
increases significantly. This is because individual SELECTs would have to be executed
against the check table, and they are not supported by a database index. In addition,
the check only usually makes sense in terms of content if it refers to the first primary
key field (after the client) in the check table. In most cases, such fields are then part of
a foreign key check, which means they are better covered in terms of content and
runtime. Checks are aborted due to this criterion right at the start (after buffering has
been attempted) and do not provide any results.

=====PAGE 1143=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1143
Replace value table checks (VTC) with foreign key checks (FKC) (enabled by default).
If this option is active, when the worklist is created, the application checks whether
value table checks are also covered by a foreign key check against the same table. If
this is the case, the value table check is not executed. This removes a redundancy from
the worklist without negatively impacting the result. Checks that are not executed due
to this behavior are not included in the worklist. They are therefore not visible in the
DCV monitor and in the results evaluation.
Furthermore, foreign key checks that are identical to value table checks are automatically omitted.
In addition, date fields and time fields are always ignored for foreign keys. Time fields are ignored
because time windows cannot be validated correctly against the validity period of master data
records in terms of content. A check for equality is not appropriate here and, for an interval check,
certain field names are missing in foreign key definitions.
The Data Consistency Verification execution depends on which foreign keys are defined in the
SAP® Data Dictionary, in the customizing table /SNP/FK01FKEYDEF and which fixed values and
value tables are defined in domains. If neither a foreign key nor a domain is defined, no check takes
place – at least in the current version.
Data Consistency Verification enables you to run tests quickly and fully automatically. DCV there-
fore plays a key role in giving table-based data migrations a similar security standard to that of
migrations via postings (BAPIs). At the same time, the advantages it provides in terms of the flex-
ibility and runtime of the migration are fully preserved.
12.3.20 Foreign Key Finder
The foreign key finder is an enhancement of the foreign key check and can be used to find and eval-
uate suggestions for foreign key relationships.
The Data Consistency Verification checks by default the SAP® Data Dictionary and foreign keys
that are only defined by table relationships in the SAP® standard. However, many table rela-
tionships are not defined in the standard. In this case, the foreign key finder suggests the missing
foreign key relationships.

12.3.21 Defining Additional Foreign Keys
In Data Consistency Verification, you can create and maintain additional foreign key definitions.
This allows you to extend the consistency checks based on the local SAP® Data Dictionary. The
existing DCV check algorithms from both the SAP® S/4HANA engine and AnyDB engine are then
applied to the newly defined foreign keys.
The foreign key definitions can have three origins:
SAP definitions
SNP definitions
Custom definitions

=====PAGE 1146=====
1146
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
The standard SAP definitions are from the latest releases. SNP definitions are created by SNP
employees in software development systems. The data correlation analysis used for this purpose is
executed with the Foreign Key Finder (transaction /N/SNP/DCV_FKF).

eign key check algorithms and supplement them with custom definitions. These foreign key defin-
itions are later used in the regular DCV run (/N/SNP/DCV) (see chapter Data Consistency
Verification).

12.3.24 Executing Data Consistency Verification Without Changing
the Target System
This chapter shows how to validate migrated data against customizing data and master data before
importing it into the target system of a transformation project. Two approaches are compared: a
check of Staging data and a classic import. The comparison shows that both lead to the same
check results.
12.3.24.1 Data Quality
The quality of the data validation before the import is determined by the following factors:
Ensuring data consistency
Reducing errors
Ensuring that the target system works after the migration
Due to the import into Staging, it is possible to use Data Consistency Verification earlier, more fre-
quently and for small test migrations of individual data objects during test cycles. This increases the
quality of mappings and conversion rules faster and more efficiently than if Data Consistency Veri-
fication is executed only after extensive test migrations.
12.3.24.2 Business Cases
Downtime Optimization: Reduces the downtime during deletion operations and provides a paper
bin function for data recovery.
System conversion Downtime Optimization: Reduces the downtime during system conversions.
An additional target system is required, and the conversion cannot be performed within the same
production system.
Data Consistency Verification without import: Enables you to execute Data Consistency Veri-
fication without an import into the target system. This eliminates the need to rebuild the target

=====PAGE 1150=====
1150
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
system, which allows faster and more frequent operations and testing in both early and late project
phases. It does not interfere with other tests or data.
Data change recording and rollback: Records data changes during migration and allows you to
roll them back. This improves traceability.
12.3.24.3 Staging Log
The advantage of the Staging log is that multiple source systems can be migrated on weekends.
The Staging log can identify data as well as the respective source systems to which the data is
assigned. This function is useful for managing data from multiple source systems in a single migra-
tion project. In addition, the Staging log is an important tool for identifying data that has been suc-
cessfully imported into the target system. Furthermore, the Staging log can identify data that has
not been imported due to issues such as duplicate keys.
Another important feature of the Staging log is the ability to identify inconsistencies within the impor-
ted data in a single run, without the need for subtractions. This is especially useful if Data Con-
sistency Verification was not executed before the import. In such scenarios, the Staging log can
distinguish between the newly imported data and the data that is already in the system. This makes
it easier to execute Data Consistency Verification.
12.3.24.4 Example: Staging Data with the Classic Approach
12.3.24.4.1 Into Staging Scenario:
In the Into Staging scenario, the Transformation Cockpit is first prepared for the data migration pro-
cess. This includes selecting a specific data object and performing an export in the background.
Then the import is started in Staging mode, so that the data can be moved into the temporary Sta-
ging area.
Once the data has been imported into the Staging area, a check is performed to ensure that the
data has been imported correctly. To do so, a new session is started on the target system, and the
name of the shadow table is retrieved via transaction /SNP/SG_LOCATION. The existence of the
shadow table and its records is then checked.
The next step is to execute Data Consistency Verification for the Staging table. This DCV run is
called Review of Staging data. Several settings are selected that apply specifically to data from
Staging. Once the processing is complete, the results are checked for possible inconsistencies.

=====PAGE 1151=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1151
After executing Data Consistency Verification and verifying the results, the Staging table is deleted
via transaction /SNP/SG.
12.3.24.4.2 Classic Scenario:
This scenario starts with disabling the import in Staging mode. This returns the system to its ori-
ginal state. Data Consistency Verification is executed before the regular import. It has the run
description Record existing inconsistencies before import. The data is then imported directly into
the target system without Staging. After that, the imported data is checked to ensure that the new
records have been added to the target table.
After the import, Data Consistency Verification is executed again. It has the description Record
inconsistencies after import. The results of this run are then compared with the results before the
import. This takes place via transaction /SNP/DCV_SUBTRACT. This comparison helps to identify
inconsistencies that might have occurred during the import.
The goal of both scenarios Into Staging and Classic is to find and fix the same inconsistencies.
This ensures the integrity of the data migration process.

12.5 Validation Reports
Validation reports aim to reduce the time needed for validation (after a migration) to a minimum.
The general idea of validation reports is to compare the contents of SAP standard reports after a
migration to ensure that the transformation was successful. These are mainly well-known reports
from the FI, MM and CO modules. Once the comparison is complete, the corresponding task dis-
plays the results in the Description tab. If conflicts occur, a ticket is created, and the issues that are
found are displayed in bar charts. This gives you an overview of the issues that have occurred and
allows you to view the overlaps and/or the missing or differing records row by row. For each row in

=====PAGE 1157=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1157
the report, a key is specified that matches its counterpart. The key also serves as a caption for the
individual rows. After the task is executed, the spool lines are converted into nodes in a tree struc-
ture. The columns of the report become the attributes of the nodes.
You can find the validation reports in Mission Control in the S4B Unit template within the Trans-
formation phase in the Verification summary task.
12.5.1 How It Works
The Verification summary task contains the general task Define parameters for reports and one
summary task per SAP (sub)module. Three child tasks are located below each summary task in
each SAP (sub)module.
Task
Description
Define parameters for
reports
Define parameters for executing the reports
Run <report> in source
Retrieve spool file of a report from the source system
Run <report> in target
Retrieve spool file of a report from the target system
Compare results auto-
matically
Compare generated spool files with each other
NOTE
On SAP systems with version 4.6c or older, you must perform
this comparison manually.
NOTE
You can find more detailed information about the tasks in the chapter Tasks in Kyano
Mission Control.
The entire process is based on a configuration that is defined for each report in order to determine
all the information displayed in the spool file. This configuration is created using regular expres-
sions to search the files for different search patterns. You can also specify other properties to
determine behavior in certain situations, such as nodes with duplicate keys that you want to merge
into a single node and whose numerically defined values are aggregated.

12.5.3 Normalizing Spool Data
12.5.3.1 Layouts for the Report Display
Reports are parsed and compared using a configuration that relies on the specific layout /SNP_
TBONE developed by SNP. This is used when executing the tasks that call the spool files in Kyano
Mission Control.
NOTE
For the reports RFSOPO00 (General ledger line items) and RAGITT_ALV01 (Asset his-
tory sheet), additional tasks exist to define the SNP layout as default. Additionally, a
task exists to reset the user’s layout, because this option is not available in their selec-
tion screen.
12.5.3.2 Converting Values to Internal Format
For numeric fields: The tool transfers the values from the files and applies logic to convert
them to the internal format without thousands separators.
For fields with conversion routines:
Conversion in the control system: For certain areas such as LIFNR, KUNNR, BELNR,
etc., conversions must not take place in the system from which the data originates,
because it uses the general standard function module EXIT_CONVERSION_ALPHA_
INPUT.
Conversion in satellite systems: Certain domains like MATNR can have a specific con-
version routine per system. Therefore, the tool collects all values and then calls an RFC
to convert all values.
12.5.3.3 Collection of ambiguous nodes:
This function is defined by the level in the configuration. It collects ambiguous key nodes (rep-
resented by the heading), aggregates their numeric fields and concatenates character-like values
separated by commas.
You can trigger the function as follows:

=====PAGE 1161=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1161
Via certain reports that cannot define a unique key due to missing data.
When a merge profile is used for the assignment and the assigned value is part of the head-
ing (key).
12.5.4 Understanding How Transformation Cockpit Mappings Work
12.5.4.1 Determining Mapping Candidates
If only one mapping can be used for a certain area, the tool selects it and assigns the values
to the file.
If more than one option exists for a certain area, a ticket is created to allow the user to select
the mapping they want to use.
The results document contains a section that displays the current mapping selection by
domain.
The assignments can be retrieved from the target system. This also includes automatically
added assignments (i.e. assignments created by an import into Transformation Cockpit) to
the assignment table. You can enable or disable this function at any time for each inde-
pendent domain by using the same ticket that you used to select the mapping.
The number of entries of the selected mapping is displayed in the mapping selection ticket.
This number also takes the mappings from the target system into account, if enabled.
12.5.4.2 Mapping Value Match Function 
You can choose from two different methods, a precise method and an approximate method.
Precise method:
If the mapping structure includes dependent fields, they can be used for the comparison if
they were found in the processed node or in its parent tree branch.
Approximate method:
This method is generally used if the precise method does not lead to a result.
It filters the table of assignment values according to the dependent fields found in the pro-
cessed node or its parent tree branch.
It determines all dependent fields.
Subsequently, adjacent duplicate entries are deleted, taking into account the main source
and target fields.
Result (in the detailed comparison report):

=====PAGE 1162=====
1162
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
If the method finds only one matching entry, the target assignment value is defined for the
node and describes the assignment in the attribute MAP_DESCRIPTION.
In the case of an assignment with dependent fields: The assignment function issues a mes-
sage in the field MAPPING_ERROR if:
The configuration is set to Strict.
The report row has more than one value that could serve as a dependent value.
It is not specified in the configuration which field is supposed to apply this function.
EXAMPLE
If a report row contains two plants and one storage location. If the plant to be
taken into account is not specified when processing the storage location assign-
ment, the process issues this message.
The message in the field MAPPING_ERROR indicates that there is an ambiguity regarding
the dependent fields.
If the mapping mode is set to Soft, this message is not displayed.
If no match exists, the value remains unchanged.
The field MAP_DESCRIPTION contains the concatenated values of all assignments made
for the node.

This ticket is filled if more than one Transformation Cockpit mapping is found for a domain. You can
