12.5.7 Tickets for Validation Reports
If conflicts occur while executing the Compare results automatically task, they are attached to the
task as a ticket. The ticket contains information about which records were found during the file com-
parison that match, do not match, or are missing from one of the files. A chart graphically displays
this information.
NOTE
All tickets for a task are available in the Tickets tab of the task. All tickets for all child
tasks below a summary task are available in the Tickets tab of the summary task.
Double-click a ticket to obtain more information.
12.5.7.1 Ticket Types
Once you have executed the task for comparing the result files, a ticket is created if there are dif-
ferences or conflicts. The ticket displays an overview of the results and shows them as charts. By
default, the charts only show differences. However, differences and absolute values can also be dis-
played if the parameter P_DIFF (Show only differences?) is set as initial in the API program. You
can download the results in the Documents tab.

12.5.9 Upgrading Configuration Tables
In the configuration tables /SNP/CW00VRCFG* for validation reports, the Profile key field is avail-
able. It allows the user to create their own report configuration profile and add the desired report
configurations to this newly created profile.
If you were using an older product version before the upgrade, the newer version will also be
installed. During this process, the upgrade function triggered once by the comparison API program
/SNP/CW02_VR_API_SPL_HIER_CMP, creates a new profile called SNP_CUST. It contains the
previously delivered report configurations that were not assigned to a profile.
NOTE
This allows you to continue using the changed configurations.
After the upgrade, two report configuration profiles are now available (SNP and SNP_CUST) with
previous versions. If you install the latest product version for the first time, only the SNP profile will
be displayed.
The process will log this activity in the execution log on the first comparison task to be executed.

13 Automated Testing
13.1 About the Automated Testing
Automated Testing focuses on checks using SAP® standard functions (BAPIs) and transactions.
Individual checks are also possible (e.g. whether mandatory fields are filled, whether hidden fields
are empty, etc.).
Use Automated Testing to:
Check your application data and Customizing settings after a system transformation (e.g.
data migration or system upgrade).
Assess side effects after a system change (e.g. Customizing or program change).
Execute mass tests of SAP® application data as regression tests.
Create automated tests for SAP® application data without significant initial effort.
13.2 Roles and Authorizations
The currently valid role overview is available in the chapter Roles and Authorizations for the SNP
Software Components AN, TF and MC.
NOTE
To perform a migration in the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit, you require the authorization
object FINS_MIG with the activity 16.
NOTE
In order to generate and activate CDS views in the SNP S/4HANA Cockpit, you require
the authorization object S_DEVELOP.

13.5 Best Practices
This chapter provides best practices for Automated Testing.
13.5.1 Execution Order
NOTE
We recommend running DCV first to find the more serious errors. After that, execute
Automated Testing to find errors that are more difficult to detect. It does not make sense
to execute both products at the same time.
13.6 Administration and Global Settings
This chapter provides information on administrating Automated Testing.
WARNING
Only execute these functions if you are properly trained in using Automated Testing. If you
use these functions incorrectly, you risk disabling the production check and changing data
on production systems.
Proceed as follows to manage global settings:
NOTE
If you make any changes after loading the test objects, you must reload them.
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/AT75_ADMIN.
The Global settings program opens.
2. In the area Set global settings for loading check functions, adjust your desired settings:
Check functions for customers: Select this option to enable the check functions that are
released for customers.
Check functions for projects: Select this option to enable the check functions that are relea-
sed for projects. Only SNP consultants should use these check functions in projects.

=====PAGE 1175=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1175
Check functions in development: Select this option to enable the check functions that are
still in development.
WARNING
Do not use the check functions in development in projects, because they can still
contain errors.
3. Settings for editing check functions: Select the function Selections can be changed to
change the selection modules in transaction /N/SNP/AT75_MAINT_OBJ.
4. Settings for productive systems: Select the option Deactivate productive check to switch
off the productive check.
WARNING
Only enable this function on test systems that are still defined as production sys-
tems for technical reasons. Do not under any circumstances use this function on
production systems, because you might create and change data on these sys-
tems.
5. Settings for parallelization: Select the option Processes are parallelized to specify the num-
ber of processes you want to use for processing a test object in transaction /N/SNP/AT75_
CHECK.
NOTE
When test objects are parallelized, lock problems can occur if two test objects att-
empt to access the same data record.
6. Settings for creation checks: Select the option Simulation is changeable to choose whether
you want to switch off simulation mode when starting test objects. If you switch off the simu-
lation, data is created and saved on the system during the test run.
7. Click
Execute.
You have saved your settings.
You will receive a message in the status bar.

You have the option to start the execution of saved program variants of transaction /N/SNP/AT75_

more information, see Saved Protocols.

NOTE
The program variants must have been previously saved in transaction
/N/SNP/AT75_CHECK.

a.

13.9.1 Before the Migration

DATA_FOR_AT is set and that the code for the function is available.

Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation Release 17.03 SP03 or higher has been installed on the
source, target and control systems.
Automated Testing 17.06 or higher has been installed on the target system.
Proceed as follows to prepare Automated Testing for testing the migration scope:
1. Log on to the control system.
2. Start transaction /N/SNP/TC.

13.12.6 Redefining Messages
What Is a Message Redefinition?
A message redefinition is the conversion of a message that normally would appear during
the runtime of a check module. You can use a redefinition to prevent such a message appea-
ring in the run log. However, it is also possible to redefine the message type so that, for exam-
ple, an error message is reclassified as a warning.
Maintaining Message Redefinitions
Proceed as follows to maintain a message redefinition:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/AT75_REDEF_MSG.
2. You can create, change and delete message redefinitions.
A distinction is made between SNP records and customer records. SNP records can-
not be changed or deleted. SNP records are indicated by
and customer records by
.
Creating Message Redefinitions

=====PAGE 1206=====
1206
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
Proceed as follows to create a message redefinition:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/AT75_REDEF_MSG.
2. In the toolbar of the ALV grid, click
Create redefinition.
3. Enter the message class, the message number and a reason in the designated fields.
4. Depending on the type of redefinition you want, specify whether you want to change
the message type, hide the message or define a function module for the message
redefinition.
NOTE
If you define a function module for the message redefinition, this function
module must already exist. To create a function module for the message
redefinition, you can use the function module /SNP/AT75_EXAMPLE_
MSGREDEF as a template.
5. Click
Continue.
The message redefinition is saved as customer record.

13.13 Limitations
It is not possible to execute this application on productive systems. You can create and edit
data on the system by carrying out a test run.
Due to enhancements on your system, the delivered tests might not be fully applicable.
Errors can occur due to incomplete batch input sessions, for example.
NOTE
This product's scope does not include adapting tests to your system environment.
Automated Testing provides a basis for automated SAP® application tests.
NOTE
The standard delivery does not provide for complete test coverage.

=====PAGE 1210=====

User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
Field
Possible values
The following values can be maintained:
SIGN is of data type c and length 1. For each line, the con-
tent of SIGN determines whether the result of the line con-
dition will be included or excluded in the overall result amount
for all lines. The possible values are I and E.
I signifies Inclusive (criterion for inclusion)
E signifies Exclusive (criterion for exclusion)
OPTION is of data type c and length 2. OPTION contains the
selection operator. The following operators are available:
If HIGH is empty, EQ, NE, GT, LE, LT, CP and NP can
be used. The operators are the same as for logical
expressions. However, the operators CP and NP do not
have the full range of functions found in normal logical
expressions. They are only allowed if wildcard cha-
racters ('*' or '+') are used in the input fields. If wildcard
characters are used on the selection screen, the ope-
rator CP is used automatically. The symbol # is defined
as the escape character.
If HIGH is filled, BT and NB can be used. These ope-
rators correspond to BETWEEN and NOT BETWEEN
when checking if a field belongs to an interval. No wild-
card characters can be used.
LOW has the same data type as the column of the database
table to which the selection criterion is linked.
If HIGH is left empty, the content of LOW defines a sin-
gle field comparison. In connection with the operator in
the OPTION field, the interval specifies a condition for
the database selection.
If HIGH is filled, the content of LOW and HIGH spe-
cifies the upper and lower limits for an interval. In
connection with the operator in the OPTION field, the
interval specifies a condition for the database selection
(interval selection).

=====PAGE 1211=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1211
Field
Possible values
HIGH has the same data type as the column of the database
table that is linked to the selection criterion. The content of
HIGH specifies the upper limit for an interval selection.

The window Create object catalog entry opens.
13. Specify a package for storing the test configuration.
NOTE
It is also possible to save the test configuration as a local object.
You have created a test configuration. You can now maintain and execute this test con-
figuration in Solution Manager.
13.15.3 Maintaining Test Configurations in Solution Manager
Proceed as follows to maintain and use a test configuration in Solution Manager:
1. Start transaction SOLAR02.
2. Select a process step and switch to the Test Cases tab.
3. Click
Add.
A row is added to the table.
4. Enter the following data in the row:
Select the test case type Ecatt Test Configuration.
Enter a source component.
Select the desired test case.
Select the desired variant.
5. Save your entries.
You can now execute the test case or integrate it into your test plans.
13.16 Maintenance
SNP Schneider-Neureither & Partner SE does not maintain tests developed by customers.
If errors within the test run logic occur due to customer enhancements, these errors do not fall
within the scope of the maintenance.
Adjustments to the check logic in the customer's system environment do not fall within the
scope of the maintenance.

14 Cross-component Topics
In this section, you will find topics that affect several SNP software components equally.
14.1 Collecting Usage Statistics
Usage Statistics Collection is an SNP software component used to collect information about the
usage of other SNP software components. It is enabled by default. The information collected does
not relate to users or their behavior. It does not contain any personal data. It only indicates how
many times the various aspects of the SNP software are used. The collected data is available in the
/SNP/US00STAT database tables.
The collected statistics are not automatically transferred to SNP. They will be downloaded later
using transaction /N/SNP/US_EXPORT. When using SNP software components, automated col-
lection is scheduled two days in advance at 04:00 am by default. You can disable the automated
collection in the table /SNP/US0XPARAMS or via transaction /N/SNP/US_PARAMS.
14.1.1 Executing Usage Statistics Collection
In addition to automatic data entry, you can also enter data manually.
The user role /SNP/US_46C_EDIT is enabled for automated collection.
Usage Statistics Collection is performed only on control systems. In a future release, Usage
Statistics Collection will also be available for usage statistics from remote systems.
Usage statistics are supported only for releases 7.01 and higher.
14.1.1.0.1 Running Usage Statistics Collection Manually
NOTE
You require the user role /SNP/US01_DIALOG.
Proceed as follows to execute the Usage Statistics Collection manually: 
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/US.
The Usage statistic collector window opens.
2. Optional: Adjust the Number of processes.
3. Click
Execute.
The data is collected with the specified number of processes.

=====PAGE 1214=====
1214
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
14.1.1.0.2 Scheduling and Executing the Usage Statistics Collection Auto-
matically
NOTE
You require the user role /SNP/US_46C_EDIT.
Proceed as follows to schedule and execute the Usage Statistics Collection automatically:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/US_PARAMS.
2. Click
Display -> Change.
3. In the area AUTO_JOB_SCHEDULING, specify the parameter value X to enable the auto-
mated data collection. Delete the X to disable the function. The data collection is enabled by
default.
4. You can use the following additional functions if the parameter is enabled:
Optional: In the area AUTO_JOB_TIME, specify when you want to collect the data.
The standard time is 04:00 am.
Optional: In the area AUTO_JOB_DAYS_AHEAD, specify the number of days on
which you want to collect data.
WARNING
Do not delete the record with this parameter. Otherwise, when using the
SNP components, it will be recreated with the default value.
Optional: In the area HIT_COUNTER, specify the parameter value X to enable the
counter for SNP software components when the user executes a transaction. Delete
the X to disable the function. The counter is enabled by default.
5. Click
Change -> Display to save your changes.
The data is collected automatically according to your specification.
14.1.2 Downloading Usage Statistics Collection Data
After the required data has been collected by the Usage Statistics Collection, you can save it
locally.
Proceed as follows to download data:
1. Start transaction /N/SNP/US_EXPORT.
The Save as window opens.

=====PAGE 1215=====
User Guide – CrystalBridge® Transformation
1215
2. In the Save in: field, select the desired folder.
3. Enter a file name.
4. Select *ZIP as the file type.
5. Click Save.
The data was saved locally.
14.1.3 Using the Usage Statistics Collection
The Usage Statistics Collection is a tool designed to collect information about the usage of SNP
software components. The collected data is useful for the following tasks, for example:
Identifying frequently used software components for which development effort should be
increased.
Identifying unused software components to increase their business value based on employee
training or improvement as well as further development, for example.

14.2 Roles and Authorizations for the SNP Software Components AN, TF, MC and SHC
14.2.1 Composite Roles
Composite roles allow you to easily assign all necessary SAP authorizations that are required to use Kyano CrystalBridge Transformation and Kyano
CrystalBridge Analysis. When assigning roles to users, composite roles are recommended in order to keep the effort to a minimum. If the customer or
SAP administrators need to further restrict authorizations, single roles can be used instead of composite roles (see below).
Name
Description
/SNP/TF_DIA_ALL
Composite role for dialog users on control and satellite systems for using TF and AN
/SNP/TF_RFC
Composite role for RFC users on control and satellite systems for using TF and AN
Composite roles do not include roles that are delivered separately (see roles in the list below, e.g. /SNP/XX_MIG_755_RFC, /SNP/TF_TC_PP_SAT_
754_ALL). These must be installed and assigned separately.
